items.title: Tomate : le Maroc devance de nouveau l'Espagne dans l'UE
items.description: Deuxième fournisseur de tomates de l'Union européenne en 2025/2026, le Royaume passe devant l'Espagne pour la deuxième année d'affilée. Sur dix campagnes, ses exportations ont progressé de plus de 22%, alors que celles de ses concurrents ibérique et néerlandais ont reculé. Sur le marché européen de la tomate, le rapport de forces continue de pencher en faveur du Maroc. Lors de la campagne 2025/2026, le Royaume a écoulé dans l'Union européenne (UE) des volumes supérieurs à ceux de l'Espagne, ce qui se produit pour la deuxième année consécutive. Ce constat ressort d'une analyse du site spécialisé Hortoinfo, qui s'appuie sur les données du service statistique Euroestacom (Icex-Eurostat). Le Maroc conforte ainsi sa deuxième place parmi les fournisseurs de l'Union, derrière les Pays-Bas. Cette performance s'inscrit dans une dynamique de fond. Si l'on compare la campagne 2025/2026 à celle de 2016/2017, les expéditions marocaines vers l'UE affichent une hausse de 22,17%, passant de 403.798 à 493.327 tonnes. Sur la même période, les ventes espagnoles ont reculé de 36,99%, revenant de 755.175 à 475.803 tonnes, et celles des Pays-Bas de 18,4%, de 947.852 à 773.449 tonnes. Pour cette campagne, les États membres ont acheté plus de 2,78 millions de tonnes de tomates, pour une facture dépassant 5,56 milliards d'euros. Le prix moyen payé ressort à deux euros le kilo. À titre de comparaison, le volume total importé atteignait 3,07 millions de tonnes en 2016/2017, soit un recul global de 9,33% en dix campagnes. Les Pays-Bas restent en tête du classement, malgré leur repli sur dix campagnes. Leurs exportateurs ont placé 773.450 tonnes, soit 27,81% du volume total importé, pour une valeur de plus de 1,64 milliard d'euros. Le kilo s'est vendu en moyenne à 2,13 euros. Le Maroc vient juste derrière, avec 493.330 tonnes, soit 17,74% du volume total. Ces ventes ont généré 1,03 milliard d'euros, sur la base d'un prix moyen de 2,09 euros le kilo. L'Espagne talonne son voisin du sud avec 475.800 tonnes, soit 17,11% du volume global, pour 1,01 milliard d'euros. Son prix moyen, de 2,14 euros le kilo, dépasse celui obtenu par les producteurs marocains. Le Portugal occupe la quatrième place avec 175.020 tonnes, pour 117,58 millions d'euros seulement. Son prix moyen, de 0,67 euro le kilo, est nettement inférieur à celui de ses concurrents, car l'essentiel de ses livraisons concerne des tomates destinées à l'industrie. Ses ventes ont toutefois bondi de 171,02% depuis 2016/2017. La France complète le top 5 avec 160.750 tonnes, pour une valeur de 373,31 millions d'euros. Ses ventes ont cédé 13,53% sur dix campagnes, mais elle affiche le prix moyen le plus élevé des cinq principaux fournisseurs, à 2,32 euros le kilo. Derrière ce quintette, la Turquie a livré 148.411 tonnes (5,34% du total), en hausse de 49,68% sur dix campagnes, devant la Belgique avec 141.470 tonnes, en recul de 26,24%. L'Allemagne et l'Italie ont respectivement fourni 104.768 et 68.349 tonnes, tandis que la Tunisie, avec 38.918 tonnes, a vu ses volumes multipliés par plus de quatre (+310,85%). The post Tomate : le Maroc devance de nouveau l'Espagne dans l'UE appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all territory seized by Houthis
items.description: Yemen’s leader announced on Sunday the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the group made fresh gains on the ground, effectively encircling a government-held city. The announcement sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost swathes of the country’s Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait — a chokepoint for international shipping — after a lightning offensive by Houthis. Yemen’s government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia, where the Houthis said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital yet again on Sunday. “I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory,” Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a statement. Alimi called on all the armed forces “to begin carrying out their assigned missions, in accordance with the approved plans, until the country is liberated from the grip of the Houthi terrorist militia”. The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government’s interim capital Aden, according to four security sources. The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around Taiz, where dozens of combatants were reported killed on Friday. The battle for Taiz is taking place on several fronts, including highlands overlooking coastal areas recently seized by the Houthis. Taiz is Yemen’s third-largest city after Sanaa and Aden. “We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station,” a police source in the area told AFP . Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city. The military sources added that fighting in the area was ongoing. Sources from both sides told AFP on Sunday that fighting in and around the western province of Taiz has killed more than 70 people over the past day. Sources from the internationally recognised government reported that 34 government troops were killed — 20 on the edge of Taiz province in neighbouring Lahj — while Houthi military sources said 39 of their fighters were killed in fighting across Taiz and in border areas with Lahj. Taiz city itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen’s long-running civil war. “They’ve achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven’t fully taken control of it,” Farea Al-Muslimi, research fellow at the Chatham House think-tank, told AFP . Muslimi also downplayed expectations over what the coming government offensive might accomplish. “In my opinion, it’s meaningless,” he added. But Taiz residents vowed to resist any Houthi advance. “We will defeat and crush anyone who enters the city of Taiz. We will not abandon Taiz,” resident Zakaria Al-Dhubhani said. “This is a message to the Houthis: I swear to God, we will not allow you to advance a single inch into the city.” Saudi attacks Following several years of relative calm, Yemen’s civil war reignited in July against the backdrop of the wider conflict in the Middle East. It has also drawn in Saudi Arabia — leader of an anti-Houthi military coalition since 2015 — with the group regularly claiming attacks on the kingdom’s territory in recent weeks and declaring a blockade of its ships in the Red Sea. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree on Sunday said the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi energy giant Aramco’s sites in Riyadh and in the oil-rich Khurais area in the east. “The strikes were precise, causing large fires at the targeted sites,” Saree said on X. Saudi oil exports were already under pressure thanks to Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf. The Houthis’ Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes on Sunday in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded. They came a day after Yemen’s government said its forces struck Houthi targets around the country, including in the capital Sanaa, the northwestern governorate of Saada and the group’s positions near Taiz in the southwest. The Yemeni government’s air capabilities, however, are limited, and the Saudi-led coalition has long been the primary force carrying out airstrikes against the Houthis. Experts believe the recent operations have most likely been conducted by Saudi warplanes as well. Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis that has unspooled since the civil war broke out in 2014. That year the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-led government, before going on to take control of much of the country’s north, with Riyadh’s international coalition intervening the following year. Hunger warning Hostilities between the Houthis and Yemen’s government had reignited after four years of a fragile truce when Iran sent a plane to Sanaa carrying a Houthi delegation. The flight did not seek authorisation from Saudi Arabia, contravening a practice in place for a decade. Riyadh retaliated with strikes on Sanaa airport, and in response the Houthis attacked Saudi territory for the first time since 2022. Since then, fighting has intensified with the Houthis launching a lightning offensive in which they seized control of coastal regions along the Bab al-Mandab strait. They have also struck multiple Saudi targets including oil infrastructure and the capital Riyadh while also announcing a naval blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea. The renewed fighting has worsened a humanitarian crisis sweeping Yemen, with the World Food Programme warning on Friday that three-quarters of the population was unable to meet its basic food needs.

items.title: Labé : un boulanger retrouvé mort dans la brousse à Dionfo, les circonstances du décès restent floues
items.description: Un boulanger identifié comme Mamadou Saïdou Diallo, âgé d’une quarantaine d’années, a été retrouvé mort dans la nuit du samedi 3 au dimanche 4 octobre 2026, dans des circonstances qui restent encore à élucider. Selon les informations recueillies, c’est aux environs de 23 heures que la victime aurait lancé des cris de détresse avant de disparaître. Après plusieurs heures de recherches, son corps a finalement été retrouvé dans la brousse. Les faits se sont produits dans le village de Gobia, situé dans le district de N’Deylal, relevant de la commune rurale de Dionfo, dans la préfecture de Labé. Mamadou Siradio, président du district de N’Deylal, revient sur les circonstances du drame : « C’était pendant la nuit. J’étais déjà couché lorsque le chef de secteur est venu m’informer que le boulanger qui travaille ici avait lancé des cris, mais qu’il restait introuvable. Nous nous sommes alors mobilisés pour organiser les recherches. Nous avons découvert des traces de sang et avons poursuivi les recherches jusqu’à retrouver son corps dans la brousse. Il était blessé à la main. Comme personne parmi nous n’était habilité à toucher au corps, nous avons informé les autorités. » D’après le président du district, la victime, originaire de Singhouma, serait âgée de 45 à 47 ans. Elle était mariée à deux femmes et père de plusieurs enfants. « Nous avons informé les autorités depuis hier soir et nous attendons leur arrivée. Le corps se trouve toujours sur place. Nous demandons aux autorités de retrouver le ou les auteurs de cet acte inhabituel dans notre localité. Nous sommes inquiets », a-t-il ajouté. Pour l’heure, les circonstances exactes de ce décès ainsi que les causes de la mort restent à déterminer. Une enquête devrait permettre de faire la lumière sur les circonstances dans lesquelles le boulanger a trouvé la mort. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Labé : un boulanger retrouvé mort dans la brousse à Dionfo, les circonstances du décès restent floues est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: North Darfur: Aid needs mount as 1,400 displaced reach Tawila in five days
items.description: Aid needs are mounting as new arrivals swell the population of internally displaced people in Tawila in North Darfur. Almost 1,400 people from 260 families — mostly women, children, and older people fleeing deteriorating security, food shortages, drought, low rainfall, and worsening famine conditions — have arrived in Tawila, North Darfur in just five days, bringing the number of arrivals since September 1, 2026 to more than 6,000, the General Coordination for Refugees and Displaced Persons says. Adam Rijal, the organisation’s spokesperson, tells Radio Dabanga that the latest arrivals came from various parts of North Darfur. Most are women, children, and older people fleeing deteriorating security, food shortages, drought, low rainfall, and worsening famine conditions. Tawila under growing pressure Rijal says Tawila has become a relatively safe destination for people fleeing their homes, driving a continued influx that is placing increasing pressure on resources and services for both displaced people and the host community. The new arrivals urgently need food, medicines, clean drinking water, shelter, healthcare, sanitation, protection, and psychosocial support, with priority given to children, women, older people, and other vulnerable groups. Rijal warns that continued displacement amid severe shortages of humanitarian assistance risks worsening malnutrition and disease and leaving vulnerable people exposed. He says urgent intervention cannot be delayed. Appeal for urgent aid The General Coordination for Refugees and Displaced Persons has called on humanitarian organisations, international agencies, donors, and other relevant bodies to coordinate an urgent response and provide life-saving assistance, including food, water, healthcare, shelter, sanitation, protection, and psychosocial services. Share article The post North Darfur: Aid needs mount as 1,400 displaced reach Tawila in five days appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Osun CP deploys tactical team over cult killings
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Following recent cult-related killings in Osogbo, Osun State capital, the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, has deployed the command’s tactical teams to the metropolis to restore normalcy. The deployment followed a series of shootings allegedly linked to rival cult groups in different parts of the city. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, quoting the commissioner as describing the recent killings as “disturbing and unacceptable.” According to the statement, a cult clash occurred on October 2, 2026, around the Owo-Eba area of Osogbo, during which two persons identified as Adebayo Taoreed, aka “Small Rugged,” and Oluwaseyi Daniel, aka “OSHA,” were shot dead. The police said some other persons also sustained gunshot injuries in the incident. The statement added that on October 4, suspected cultists invaded the Arowomole area of Osogbo, where one Rasak Wahab, aka “Ojo Iku,” was shot. He was reportedly evacuated to a hospital and was responding to treatment as of Sunday. Following the incidents, Zungura directed all tactical teams of the command to relocate to the Oke-Baale area and remain there until normalcy was fully restored. The teams were also directed to conduct intelligence-led raids and operations professionally and within the ambit of the law, targeting identified cult members, criminal hideouts and other locations allegedly linked to criminal activities. The police said the cases had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department for discreet investigation. Meanwhile, the commissioner directed Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and tactical commanders to intensify patrols, gather actionable intelligence and maintain sustained security presence in identified flashpoints across the metropolis. Zungura warned cultists and their sponsors that the state would not be a safe haven for criminals involved in shootings and killings. He, however, assured residents that the command was in control of the security situation and urged them to continue their lawful activities without fear. The post Osun CP deploys tactical team over cult killings appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Midterms : Donald Trump dans le mur de sa politique
items.description: L’intervention improvisée lancée avec Israël contre l’Iran met, à un mois des élections de mi-mandat, le président américain en mauvaise posture. La frange modeste de son électorat, qui avait cru à sa promesse d’un nouvel âge d’or économique, pourrait lui faire payer de se retrouver étranglée par la hausse des prix, en particulier des carburants.

items.title: Kidnapped NYSC members still in captivity
items.description: …Police locate abductors’ camp, fear IEDs By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — Prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha highway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, are still in captivity, as security agencies intensify efforts to rescue them. The victims were among passengers travelling in two buses from Ibadan, Oyo State, to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, and Bende, Abia State, respectively, when armed men attacked the vehicles at Umunoha. The Imo State Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, said security agencies had located the hideout where the abducted prospective corps members were being held, but were exercising caution because the area was reportedly heavily mined with improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Bosso said security personnel had been following leads and acting on intelligence while combing bushes around the scene of the attack. He added that a surveillance drone had also been deployed as part of the operation. The police commissioner said, “Reliable intelligence indicates that the area around the camp of the gunmen, where the corps members are being held, is heavily mined with Improvised Explosive Devices.” He assured that security operatives were aware of the location of the abductors and their captives, adding that arrangements were being made to deploy a specialised heavy-duty armoured vehicle to breach and penetrate the camp. The abduction occurred on October 1 along the Umunoha axis of the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway. In his initial statement on the incident, the Imo State Police Public Relations Officer, Mr Henry Okoye, said the Commissioner of Police, in collaboration with sister security agencies, had deployed tactical teams and operational assets to rescue the abducted corps members and other passengers and apprehend the suspected abductors. Okoye said two buses involved in the incident had been recovered, while 10 victims were rescued at the scene. He added that the exact number of persons abducted was being verified at the time and would be made public once confirmed. “Operatives are conducting coordinated search-and-rescue operations, backed by intelligence-led tracking of the suspects,” Okoye said. He further said the affected section of the expressway had been reopened and traffic restored, while security personnel remained deployed to protect commuters. In a subsequent update, the Force Public Relations Officer, Force Headquarters, Mr Aniette Iniedu, said the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, had deployed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada, to Imo State to provide operational direction for the search-and-rescue operation. According to Iniedu, Nadada arrived in the state with two Commissioners of Police and conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the situation and the ongoing operations. He said the DIG reviewed the deployment of personnel and operational assets and issued further directives to strengthen the coordinated response. “The search-and-rescue operation has been further intensified, with additional deployments of tactical teams and operational assets across identified areas, backed by intelligence-led tracking of the suspects,” Iniedu said. The development comes amid varying reports on social media about the fate of the abducted prospective corps members. However, the latest position attributed to the state police command is that security agencies have established the location of the captives and are working on a strategy to safely access the camp. The police have not disclosed the exact number of prospective corps members still in captivity. The post Kidnapped NYSC members still in captivity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Elecciones en Brasil 2026, en vivo | Lula: “Veremos qué Brasil eligió el pueblo”. Bolsonaro: “Brasil no aguanta más”
items.description: Brasil celebra este domingo una de las elecciones presidenciales más reñidas de su historia. A sus 80 años, el izquierdista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva pelea por la reelección, en el que sería su cuarto mandato no consecutivo. Tiene enfrente al senador derechista Flávio Bolsonaro , de 45 años, hijo mayor del expresidente Jair, condenado por liderar un intento de golpe de Estado. “Brasil necesita un cambio, Brasil no aguanta más”, ha dicho Bolsonaro al votar a primera hora en Río de Janeiro. Lula, por su parte, votó minutos después en una escuela de São Bernardo do Campo, en el cordón industrial de São Paulo donde nació a la vida política. “Ya veremos qué tipo de Brasil escogió el pueblo. Estoy con mucha confianza”, ha dicho el presidente. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Nigeria owes women economy worthy of their labour – Shettima
items.description: —Flags off Community Investment Fund to empower business women across Katsina —Inaugurates several road, public transportation projects, receives decampees into APC fold By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA– THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has advocated for a conducive business environment for Nigerian women to ply their trade, saying the nation owes them an economy worthy of their labour. He noted that women should be given more space for their ambition to flourish unlike in the past when they carried heavy responsibilities with limited resources for their businesses to thrive. Senator Shettima stated this on Sunday in Katsina State when he flagged off the Community Investment Fund (CIF) disbursement in a major push for women empowerment and financial inclusion under the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up (NFWP-SU) Project at Muhammadu Dikko Stadium, Katsina. He also inaugurated 32 compressed natural gas-powered buses and 200 electric-powered tricycles under the Katsina State Comprehensive Urban Renewal Programme as well as several completed road projects undertaken to improve traffic flow, connectivity and urban mobility in state metropolis. The CIF fund disbursement, he said, answers a question that should trouble every government as it borders on how much prosperity has been postponed by asking women to work miracles with too little capital According to VP Shettima, over 40,000 women in Katsina are eligible to receive business capital after fulfilling the prescribed eligibility conditions and demonstrating satisfactory performance in their savings and group activities. Making a strong case for women empowerment, he said, “Our daughters should inherit their mothers’ determination without inheriting every obstacle their mothers endured. That is another reason to make this programme succeed. The girl who watches a business grow in her own household learns that skill can yield an income, and that ambition can survive contact with adversity. “We owe these women an economy worthy of their labour. They have carried heavy responsibilities with limited means; their ambition should now have more room to flourish. With confidence in their abilities, I hereby flag off the Community Investment Fund disbursement under the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up Project in Katsina State. May Almighty Allah bless their efforts and grant our country enduring prosperity.” The Vice President maintained that the economic reforms of administration of President Bola Tinubu must translate into stronger businesses, greater purchasing power, and an improved quality of life for Nigerians. His words: “For the administration of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, economic reform must find expression in the earning capacity of citizens. We must connect national policy to the circumstances of the trader, the producer and the service provider. “Our task is to make their effort more rewarding, so that the pursuit of national growth becomes intelligible in the accounts of an ordinary household.” Senator Shettima applauded Governor Dikko Umaru Radda’s sensitivity to what he described as an “economic necessity that reaches beyond the loudest voices,” noting that the governor’s “attention to women and vulnerable households honours an essential duty of leadership: to hear those whose difficulties seldom command a microphone.” Observing that “a government earns affection when the citizen with the least influence receives its fullest attention, he said, “Katsina’s concern for enterprise acquires deeper meaning when it reaches the woman whose ambitions have remained smaller than her abilities because her resources could carry her no further. “We should never confuse a small business with a small aspiration. The scale of an enterprise often tells us more about the owner’s access to finance than about the reach of her imagination,” he added. On the CIF design, VP Shettima said it is an empowerment programme for which training is required, explaining that “money needs knowledge and organisation to produce lasting results.” He continued: “Through Women Affinity Groups, savings and lending are linked to training, financial literacy and access to productive resources. A woman should understand the terms on which she borrows, distinguish revenue from profit and possess the confidence to question a transaction. Financial participation loses much of its value without informed judgement. “To the women participating, your savings have spoken for you. Every contribution made despite competing demands records a decision to prepare for tomorrow. Preserve that discipline as your businesses grow. Keep sound records, weigh your purchases carefully and protect the trust within your groups. The habits that qualified you for this investment will matter even more when larger sums pass through your hands.” The Vice President implored those administering the fund to ensure that eligibility remains the “basis of access, without favouritism or political interference,” pointing out that beneficiaries should understand what they receive and how the process works, while each transaction are properly documented. Earlier, Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Radda, said the state government has committed an additional N4 billion to the implementation of the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up, bringing the state’s total financial commitment to the programme to N8 billion. Governor Radda noted that the flag-off of the programme was expanding economic opportunities for women across the state with the ultimate objective of improving their livelihoods. He particularly applauded the participation of women living with hearing impairment, particularly the formation of affinity groups to enhance inclusion and describing it as one of the most encouraging developments under the programme. Governor Radda added that the state government would complement the women-focused empowerment initiative with similar interventions targeting men, stressing that empowering both men and women would strengthen household incomes and promote financial independence. For his part, the World Bank Country Director for Nigeria, Mr Matthew Verghis, said Nigerian women are already making significant contributions across various sectors of the economy and noted that closing gender gaps would require deliberate action. The World Bank Country Director commended the Federal and Katsina State Governments for identifying the economic needs of women and choosing to address them through empowerment initiatives. He also called on the private sector, community leaders and traditional institutions to support efforts aimed at expanding economic opportunities for women across the state. Earlier, Vice President Shettima inaugurated 32 compressed natural gas-powered buses and 200 electric-powered tricycles under the Katsina State Comprehensive Urban Renewal Programme. The VP also inaugurated several completed road projects undertaken to improve traffic flow, connectivity and urban mobility in Katsina metropolis. He also witnessed the reception of prominent political decampees into the All Progressives Congress, APC led by former Secretary to the Katsina State Government, Dr Mustapha Inuwa and other stalwarts including 8 National Assembly aspirants, 18 State House of Assembly aspirants and several political leaders from opposition parties. The post Nigeria owes women economy worthy of their labour – Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Diaspora Nasara Caucus congratulates Mohammed Ali Suraj, new NPP executives
items.description: The Diaspora Nasara Organiser Caucus has congratulated the newly elected National Executives of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) following the party’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi. In a statement issued on Sunday, October 4, 2026, the Caucus extended particular congratulations to Alhaji Mohammed Ali Suraj on his election as National Nasara Organiser. It also congratulated John Boadu, who was elected National Chairman, and the other newly elected executives. The Caucus recognised the following executives: National Chairman: John Boadu First Vice Chairman: Kojo Fosu Boadu Second Vice Chairman: Henry Nana Boakye Third Vice Chairman: Nana Akomea General Secretary: Justin Frimpong Kodua National Organiser: Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus-Glover National Treasurer: Alfred Kojo Thompson National Women’s Organiser: Mavis Hawa Koomson National Youth Organiser: Abanga Fuseini Yakubu National Nasara Organiser: Alhaji Mohammed Ali Suraj National Communications Director: Dennis Miracles Aboagye The Caucus commended all aspirants who participated in the elections, recognising their contributions to the party and its internal democratic process. It also called on NPP members to support the new executives and work together in a spirit of unity. The Diaspora Nasara Organiser Caucus said it looks forward to engaging constructively with the newly elected National Nasara Organiser and contributing to the continued development of the Nasara Wing. The statement was issued by Issah Ayumah, Diaspora Nasara Organiser Caucus and UK Nasara Organiser.

items.title: Tombolia : un nouveau-né retrouvé vivant dans une toilette, sa mère reste introuvable
items.description: Un nouveau-né a été retrouvé vivant dans une toilette dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche 4 octobre à Tombolia Plateau 1. Alertés par les cris du bébé, des habitants du quartier se sont mobilisés pour tenter de le sortir. Ils ont finalement dû casser une partie de l’installation à l’aide de marteaux et de pioches. Le bébé, un garçon, a ensuite été conduit à l’hôpital pour recevoir des soins. Sa mère, elle, reste introuvable. Tout commence dans la nuit. Il est environ 3 heures du matin lorsque des habitants entendent les cris d’un bébé. En se rendant sur les lieux avec des torches, ils découvrent le nouveau-né coincé dans une toilette. Mariame Camara fait partie des premières personnes à avoir été informées. « J’étais couchée, ma fille est venue me réveiller. Je suis sortie, j’ai vu les gens dehors et je me suis dirigée vers les toilettes. Lorsqu’on a mis la lumière de la torche vers la toilette, j’ai vu le bébé à l’intérieur. » Avec d’autres habitants, elle se rend alors chez le chef de quartier pour l’informer de la situation. Mais, vu l’heure, ils retournent rapidement sur les lieux. « À notre retour, mes enfants et d’autres jeunes ont cassé une partie de la toilette pour faire sortir l’enfant et ils ont réussi à l’extraire. Je l’ai emmailloté dans un pagne, après je l’ai lavé et je l’ai envoyé à l’hôpital parce qu’il saignait au niveau de son nombril. » À l’hôpital, le bébé reçoit les premiers soins. « Arrivé à l’hôpital, le médecin a pris soin de son nombril et il a coupé le frein de langue. Le bébé a pleuré. Ce petit matin encore, je l’ai lavé et nous lui avons donné du lait. » Selon Mariame Camara, les autorités du quartier ont déjà été informées. Des agents des services de sécurité se sont également rendus sur place. Pour l’instant, aucune trace de la mère n’a été retrouvée. Les personnes présentes au moment de la découverte disent ne pas savoir qui a laissé le bébé dans cette toilette ni dans quelles circonstances. Mariame Camara dit, elle, être prête à garder l’enfant. « Ce que je dirais aux femmes, si tu fais un enfant, ne le jette pas dans les toilettes. Mets-le devant la porte de quelqu’un. Jeter un enfant dans les toilettes, c’est un crime. » Elle poursuit : « Pour le moment, l’enfant se porte bien. Je compte le garder, oui, et je demande aux personnes de bonne volonté de m’aider à m’occuper de lui. Chacun peut faire un peu. » Mohamed Camara a participé à l’opération de sauvetage. Il explique avoir entendu les cris du nouveau-né aux environs de 3 heures du matin. « C’était aux environs de 3 heures 16 minutes. Nous avons entendu des cris. À l’aide des torches, nous avons vérifié et nous avons trouvé des traces de sang à terre. Nous sommes entrés dans la toilette et avons essayé de faire sortir le bébé, mais nous n’avons pas pu. » Face à la difficulté, les jeunes sont allés chercher du matériel. « Nous sommes allés chercher des marteaux et des pioches. Nous avons cassé une partie de la toilette pour ne pas blesser l’enfant et nous avons fait sortir le bébé. » Mohamed Camara affirme qu’aucune trace de la mère n’a été retrouvée sur place. « Nous n’avons vu aucune trace de la mère de l’enfant. Mais les jeunes qui étaient de l’autre côté nous ont dit qu’ils avaient entendu des bruits ici. Ils ne pouvaient pas se douter de ça parce qu’ici, c’est un passage. » Le président du conseil de quartier de Tombolia Plateau 1, Aboubacar Kanfori Sylla, indique avoir été informé peu après la découverte du bébé. « Dès que nous avons été informés, nous avons appelé monsieur le maire. Il nous a donné les instructions d’informer les services de sécurité. Le commissariat a été informé. Je suis venu sur le terrain avec les agents de la police, qui sont actuellement sur le terrain pour des enquêtes. » Le nourrisson est pour le moment resté auprès de la famille qui l’a retrouvé. « L’enfant se trouve avec la famille qui l’a retrouvé jusqu’à ce que nous recevions d’autres indications à tenir avec les autorités. Pour le moment, c’est là où nous sommes. » Le bébé, pris en charge à l’hôpital après son extraction, serait actuellement hors de danger. Les services de sécurité ont ouvert des recherches pour tenter de retrouver sa mère et établir les circonstances dans lesquelles le nouveau-né s’est retrouvé dans cette toilette. Christine Findan Kamano L’article Tombolia : un nouveau-né retrouvé vivant dans une toilette, sa mère reste introuvable est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Dr Antwi-Boasiako’s cybersecurity book showcased at UN crime prevention congress
items.description: A book documenting Ghana’s cybersecurity development, authored by former Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority, Dr Albert Antwi-Boasiako, has been exhibited at the 15th United Nations (UN) Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice in Abu Dhabi. The book “ The Republic “, a professional journey, Ghana’s cybersecurity and the making of a role model country, was among the selected publications displayed at the congress, held in the United Arab Emirates from September 26 to October 1, 2026. The event brought together more than 5,000 participants from about 97 countries, the release said. Published in November 2025, the professional autobiography traces Dr Antwi-Boasiako’s career alongside the development of Ghana’s cybersecurity institutions, policies and initiatives. It also documents the contributions of public officials, industry players and international partners to that process. The book’s selection followed a recommendation from members of the United Nations Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice (CCPCJ) community. In a letter cited in the release, the Chair of the commission’s 34th session, José Antonio Zabalgoitia, described the selected publications as accounts that highlight courage, determination and resilience, while reinforcing the pursuit of just and peaceful societies. The letter also described The Republic as a valuable addition to an exhibition intended to strengthen international cooperation in addressing public security challenges. Reacting to the selection, Dr Antwi-Boasiako credited the people and institutions whose work contributed to Ghana’s cybersecurity development. “THE REPUBLIC is a record of work that was never mine alone. It reflects the efforts of many colleagues, partners, and public service officials who helped build Ghana’s cybersecurity foundations,” he said. “To see the book being selected by the United Nations Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice was entirely unexpected, and I accept the honour on behalf of everyone who shared in that journey.” The exhibition offered delegates an opportunity to explore Ghana’s cybersecurity experience through the author’s first-hand account. Following the congress, the exhibited copy is being retained in an Abu Dhabi library as part of the CCPCJ’s historical collection, according to the release. The book explores the challenges, decisions and partnerships that shaped Ghana’s cybersecurity development, presenting lessons for policymakers, professionals and public sector leaders.

items.title: NGE demands 50% presidential threshold, faster election cases
items.description: …Calls for INEC appointment reforms, independent candidacy The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has called for far-reaching constitutional and electoral reforms, including a 50 per cent threshold for presidential elections and the resolution of electoral disputes before the swearing-in of declared winners. The Guild also called for reforms to the appointment processes for the Chairman, National Commissioners and Resident Electoral Commissioners of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), as well as State Electoral Commissioners. The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC 2026), held in Enugu from September 24 to 26, 2026. The communiqué was signed by the NGE President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh. The conference, themed, “The Ballot, the Media and the Task of Keeping Democracy Alive,” was chaired by the Obi of Onitsha, His Royal Majesty Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, while the Archbishop Emeritus of Abuja, His Eminence John Cardinal Onaiyekan, delivered the keynote address. Vice-President Kashim Shettima participated virtually as Special Guest of Honour, while Enugu State Governor, Dr Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, was the Chief Host. More than 500 editors, publishers and senior media practitioners from print, broadcast and digital platforms, as well as political, traditional, religious, academic, regulatory and development-sector leaders, attended the conference. The Guild said the conference examined challenges confronting Nigeria’s electoral democracy, particularly the threats posed by artificial intelligence, misinformation, disinformation, electoral insecurity and declining public confidence in the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to the communiqué, the ballot remained the principal instrument through which citizens exercised their sovereign will, but its value depended on credible information, public confidence in the electoral process and the assurance that votes would be properly counted and respected. The editors identified voter apathy as being influenced by factors including poor governance, electoral violence and intimidation, administrative shortcomings, declining public confidence and concerns over the relationship between electoral outcomes and subsequent judicial decisions. The Guild expressed concern over perceptions in some sections of the public that judicial interventions in electoral disputes could displace outcomes recorded at the ballot box. It, however, stressed the need to respect judicial independence while calling for electoral adjudication that is timely, transparent, predictable and impartial, with genuine electoral irregularities appropriately addressed. The editors called for electoral disputes to be resolved within appropriate timelines, preferably before the swearing-in of declared winners. They also recommended consideration of a constitutional threshold requiring a presidential candidate to secure up to 50 per cent of votes cast, with a run-off where no candidate meets the threshold. The Guild further called for a review of restrictions on ordinary voters seeking to challenge electoral results and advocated a constitutional framework that would permit independent candidacy. AI, misinformation The conference identified generative artificial intelligence, deepfakes, voice cloning and automated networks as major emerging threats to the integrity of electoral information. It warned that synthetic content could be rapidly produced and distributed in the form of fabricated election results, cloned voices of public officials, forged documents, manipulated result sheets and fake reports attributed to established media organisations. The editors said the danger extended beyond individual falsehoods to the erosion of public trust when citizens could no longer distinguish authentic information from fabricated content. The Guild consequently urged newsrooms to institutionalise fact-checking and verification systems and integrate digital verification, deepfake detection and forensic tools into their editorial workflows. It also reaffirmed the Nigerian Media Code of Election Coverage (Revised 2022), jointly endorsed by the Newspaper Proprietors’ Association of Nigeria, Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria, Nigeria Union of Journalists, Nigerian Guild of Editors, Radio, Television, Theatre and Arts Workers Union and Guild of Corporate Online Publishers. The NGE urged media organisations to adopt the Code and train journalists and other editorial staff on its provisions ahead of the 2027 elections. The Guild reaffirmed the responsibility of the media to provide accurate, verified and independent information and scrutinise governments, political parties and other centres of power. It, however, stressed that media scrutiny should not amount to suppressing legitimate achievements. The editors called for evidence-based journalism that neither exaggerates failures nor suppresses verified achievements and developments. The Guild also clarified that editorial neutrality meant impartiality among legitimate political contenders and did not require journalists to remain silent in the face of verified wrongdoing or create false equivalence between established facts and unverified claims. Election security, journalists The conference urged governments at all levels to remain transparent and accountable and cooperate with the media in the legitimate exercise of its watchdog role, including scrutiny of public programmes and expenditure. It also called on government and political actors to guarantee equitable access to media space for government and opposition voices while respecting editorial independence. The Guild declared that election security must include the safety and protection of journalists covering elections. It warned that the electoral process could not be fully transparent where journalists were threatened, attacked, obstructed or prevented from independently observing and reporting events. The NGE therefore called on security agencies and political actors to protect journalists and ensure they could perform their constitutional and professional responsibilities without intimidation. The editors also urged INEC to sustain nationwide readiness assessments, strengthen technical partnerships for cybersecurity and electoral technology, ensure the technical integrity of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and protect the institutional independence of the electoral commission. They stressed that all technology deployed in elections must remain subject to human oversight, transparency, accountability and legal verification. ‘Inform, Don’t Amplify’ The conference also addressed the challenge of reporting terrorism, acknowledging the balance between the public’s right to know about terrorist attacks and the risk that irresponsible reporting could inadvertently amplify terrorist propaganda, aid recruitment, compromise security operations or traumatise victims. It consequently endorsed the principle: “Inform, Don’t Amplify.” The Guild urged newsrooms to identify terrorist claims clearly as claims until independently verified and avoid reproducing propaganda, recruitment messages, slogans or graphic material except where there was compelling editorial justification. It resolved that acts of terrorism should be reported responsibly and accurately without giving undue publicity or oxygen to terrorist organisations or inadvertently encouraging further acts of violence. The conference reaffirmed that the media should remain “pro-Nigeria, pro-Ballot and pro-People”, rather than align itself with any political party. It stressed that the credibility of Nigeria’s democracy ultimately depended on an electoral process in which citizens could make informed choices, cast their votes freely and have confidence that their votes would be accurately counted and respected. Among the major papers presented at the conference were those by former Nigerian Bar Association President, Mazi Afam Osigwe, SAN; Professor Auwalu H. Yadudu of Bayero University, Kano; former Managing Director/Editor-in-Chief of The Guardian Newspapers, Martin Oloja; Professor Chinyere Stella Okunna of Paul University, Awka; Professor Farooq A. Kperogi of Kennesaw State University, Georgia, United States; and Dr Richard Okoye, Founder/Chief Medical Director of Save a Life Hospital. The Guild expressed appreciation to the Government and people of Enugu State for their hospitality and support, as well as speakers, presenters, panellists, sponsors and development partners whose contributions enriched the conference.. items.title: 'We are not yes-men': CM Afridi launches PTI long march to Islamabad, convoy enters Karak district
items.description: PESHAWAR/LAKKI MARWAT/DI KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday launched the PTI’s long march towards Islamabad from Lakki Marwat, saying the party would “not accept” any policy that was against the interests of the people of KP. The PTI has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the federal government, which has vowed to prevent any violent gatherings in the capital. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan. By late Sunday night, the convoy led by the KP chief minister had entered Karak district and reached Hamidan Chowk. In a post shortly before 11pm, PTI said Afridi’s convoy was en route to Karak after the KP CM addressed supporters at a roundabout located at the border between Bannu and Karak districts. Earlier in the day, Afridi reached Lakki Marwat by helicopter to lead his party’s long march, which was launched from Gandi Chowk on the Peshawar-Karachi Indus Highway. In Lakki Marwat, an AFP journalist saw thousands of people take to the streets. Many of the demonstrators carried red and green flags of the PTI, and a huge billboard affixed on the side of a truck read “release Imran Khan” and featured a picture of the beaming former prime minister. Addressing thousands of participants in Lakki Marwat, Afridi urged the public to step out of their homes for the sake of Pakistan, saying Imran, along with his wife and sisters, was in prison and they should show the world that they were the “true owners” of the country. He said the “PTI’s negotiating committee had gone to Islamabad to lower the political temperature, but those making decisions behind closed doors had sabotaged the talks. “They wanted their will to prevail in KP, but I declared that only Imran Khan’s vision and policies would be implemented here. We do not accept any policy that is not in the interest of the people of KP and the Pashtuns,” he maintained. The chief minister declared: “We are not ‘yes-men’; we are soldiers of Imran Khan, and we will carry forward his policies.” He repeatedly asked the crowd whether it supported a military operation, asking those opposed to it to raise their hands. He questioned the policy being followed to tackle terrorism, saying: “What kind of policy is this, where terrorism has persisted for 22 years?” KP CM insisted there had been peace during Imran’s government because his policies were sound, but following the “regime change operation”, terrorists were resettled, leading to “infinite terrorism”. In 2023, after his ouster, Imran had defended his government’s plan to resettle members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. “We will eradicate terrorism, and if our policy is implemented, we will restore peace within 100 days,” he claimed. He said the long march was being launched from Gandi Chowk and would conclude at another chowk. At this, the crowd shouted: “D-Chowk.” “We are a political force and a party, and those who dream of the demise of the PTI can never succeed,” he added. Afridi said the participants would leave from Gandi Chowk and their next stop would be Karak. PTI workers had started gathering at Gandi Chowk on the Peshawar-Karachi Highway on Sunday afternoon to participate in the long march . Strict security measures were in place, with a large police contingent deployed at the site along with armoured personnel carriers and bomb disposal squads. Afridi assailed for using ‘state helicopter’ A special helipad was prepared near Maidadkhel for Afridi and a video shared on social media platforms earlier showed a crowd of PTI workers gathered around it as KP’s chief executive touched down. A video shared by the PTI on its X account showed Afridi’s convoy surrounded by a large crowd of party workers and supporters. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar criticised Afridi for using a “state helicopter for a political march”. Calling the use of the helicopter a “violation of the Islamabad High Court’s orders”, he wrote on X, referring to a recent ruling that directed provincial governments to ensure that no government resources or machinery was used to facilitate any march or gathering. “Terrorism is spreading in the province and Nero is playing his flute,” Tarar quipped. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also said the use of the helicopter amounted to contempt of court by violating the IHC order. “When the chief minister himself does not uphold the court’s orders and uses state resources for political activities, what expectation can there be for his workers to abide by the law?” Kundi wrote on X. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also made a sarcastic post on X, sharing the video and saying, “Sohail Afridi sahib ’s Heli ride today from Peshawar to Lakki Marwat must have been for official work, possibly related to the security situation and counterterrorism efforts.” Special Assistant to the KP CM for Home and Tribal Affairs Tariq Saad earlier told journalists at his residence that convoys from the southern KP districts would join the “peaceful long” march at Gandi Chowk. “If workers from some southern districts, especially Tank and Waziristan, could not attend the long march today due to law and order-related curfew and other restrictions, they would join the movement on the way to Peshawar the next day,” he said. Gandapur convoy returns to DI Khan Earlier, PTI workers and supporters, led by former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, set out from Dera Ismail Khan to join the party’s long march at Lakki Marwat. However, according to Gandapur, they were forced to return from Yarik on their way because of road blockades and the prevailing law and order situation. The former KP CM insisted that the decision was taken to avoid exposing party workers to unnecessary risk, after the convoy remained stranded at Yarik for several hours. Addressing the workers at Yarik, Gandapur noted that Section 144 had been imposed in the area for three days and that the party leadership had clearly directed workers not to damage public property or engage in any activity that could worsen the situation. Gandapur told the workers that the return should not be viewed as a withdrawal from the protest movement, but as a temporary decision based on the prevailing circumstances, the safety of the workers and the instructions of the party leadership. He said the workers could again set out to join the long march if the situation improved or the party leadership issued fresh instructions. The PTI leader contended that if the party leadership called him again, he could reach the long march within two hours. He emphasised that the law and order situation did not warrant keeping a large number of workers at the site overnight. The former KP CM also told the workers that they could remain at Yarik if they wanted to, but he could not violate the instructions issued by the party leadership. He stressed that the decision taken by the senior leadership was not merely a personal decision, but one that he regarded as being in line with Imran’s instructions. However, during the address, some workers expressed disagreement with the decision to take the convoy back. They said they wanted to remain at Yarik and continue their participation in the protest for as long as the movement continued. Gandapur expressed displeasure over their position and urged them to take the practical situation on the ground into account. “TikTok-type talk” should not be made here, he told the workers, stressing that decisions had to be based on the situation on the ground. The former KP CM subsequently persuaded the workers to return, following which the convoy left Yarik for DI Khan. Before departing from DI Khan, the ex-CM stressed that the protest should remain peaceful and urged the participants to maintain discipline and refrain from violence, vandalism and confrontation with law enforcement personnel. He said the party would follow a policy of “live and let live” during the protest and directed workers not to take the law into their hands. “Those who block roads or engage in confrontation are not our workers,” Gandapur said, asking the participants to remain peaceful throughout the march. He further urged the participants to avoid any activity that could lead to clashes or damage to public or private property. The PTI’s march, being carried out to demand the release of its jailed founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan, is the latest bone of contention between the two sides. In August, the PTI announced the long march to Islamabad on Sept 27 against what it called the “illegal imprisonment” of its party founder. However, a couple of days before its scheduled long march, the party postponed the march until Oct 4 (today). Federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no option but to impose governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, citing the province’s security situation and the protest call, while PTI has warned of dire consequences if such a step was taken. After weekend talks, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah has further warned that the protesters will not be allowed to enter Islamabad. Plan for the march According to the plan for the march shared by the KP CM on X, PTI supporters from the districts of Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan and Bannu will join the long march from Lakki Marwat’s Gandi Chowk on Oct 4. The caravan will halt for the night near Karak, from where people will depart at 12:30pm the next day and stay overnight near Kohat. Then, at 12pm on Oct 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram, and Orakzai will join the convoy, which will move towards Peshawar and spend the night near Mattani. The caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar on Oct 7 afternoon. “The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange,” the KP CM said. They would then depart the Charsadda Interchange at 12:30pm on Oct 8 after people from Charsadda and Mohmand join them. Refraining from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital, Afridi said the people “of entire KP” would gather at Khairabad on Oct 8 and spend the night there. “God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there.” Ahead of the march, movement on several roads on KP has been banned under Section 144. Section 144 imposed in several KP districts Section 144 has been imposed in several districts of KP through notifications issued by the respective deputy commissioners, with restrictions on the movement of people and vehicles along specified routes, citing security and public safety concerns. In DI Khan, the movement of individuals and all types of traffic on specified roads and routes has been banned between 6am and 6pm from Oct 4 to Oct 6, citing the prevailing law-and-order situation and public safety concerns. In Upper South Waziristan, Section 144 has been imposed from Oct 3 to Oct 5, banning the movement of cargo vehicles, rickshaws and dumpers over a possible VBSB/VBIED threat in adjoining areas. In Lower South Waziristan, restrictions have been imposed under Section 144 from Oct 1 to Oct 10, banning the movement of loader rickshaws, single- and double-cabin cargo vehicles, Shahzore vehicles, Mazdas, Suzuki loaders and dumpers in Wana and Azam Warsak. The notification cited security and public safety concerns. In District Tank, restrictions on the movement of individuals and all types of traffic along specified routes have been imposed under Section 144 from 9pm on Oct 3 until noon on Oct 5. The notification cited the prevailing law-and-order situation, public safety concerns and the need to ensure the safe movement of law enforcement personnel. In Hangu, restrictions have been imposed under Section 144 from Oct 3 to Oct 6, banning the movement of individuals and all types of traffic on six routes, including the Hangu-Kohat, Hangu-Thall, Hangu Bypass and Hangu-Sumari roads. The restrictions do not apply to law enforcement agencies and emergency services, while exemptions may be granted by the district police officer or security forces.

items.title: Journée mondiale des animaux : les équidés à l’honneur à Louga
items.description: L'organisation non gouvernementale Action for working horses and donkeys (Brooke) en partenariat avec la fédération des associations paysannes de Louga (Fapal) à travers le projet « Guedaal mala », a mis à profit la journée mondiale des animaux, le dimanche 4 octobre, pour particulièrement célébrer les équidés à savoir le cheval, l'âne, le mulet. Pour El Hadji Ndiaye, le chargé de programme, cette journée revêt d'une importance capitale dans la mesure où elle a permis de contribuer à l'amélioration des conditions de vie des équidés. « Nous avons profité de l'occasion pour offrir des soins et prestations vétérinaires gratuits aux chevaux et ânes de trait notamment le déparasitage externe et interne mais aussi le parage de leurs sabots », a-t-il indiqué. Le chargé de programme a souligné que cette journée a également permis de sensibiliser les communautés sur le comportement des équidés afin de faciliter leur approche et leur manipulation. « Il faut éviter tout acte cruel ou toute brutalité envers ces animaux », a averti M. Ndiaye appelant les populations ayant des équidés difficiles à se rapprocher du projet « Guedaal mala » pour bénéficier d'un accompagnement. Présidant cette rencontre, l'adjoint au sous-préfet de Keur Momar Sarr, Mamadou Thioune a salué les initiatives entreprises par Brooke et Fapal à sensibiliser sur les bonnes pratiques d'élevage et de prise en charge des équidés en milieu rural. Le représentant de l'autorité administrative a également saisi cette tribune pour rappeler le rôle important joué par les équidés dans l'économie locale. « Ces animaux appuient les populations dans les travaux champêtres mais aussi ils assurent le transport », a-t-il fait savoir. D'où la nécessité de préserver leur bien-être, selon lui. Falel Pam

items.title: Sanwo-Olu, Adeboye urge Nigerians to serve nation
items.description: …Sowore seeks peace, progress as Nigeria marks 66th Independence By Olayinka Latona LAGOS — Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, and the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, have urged Nigerians to embrace patriotism, responsible leadership and genuine service to God and humanity as the country marks its 66th Independence anniversary. They spoke at the annual Independence Thanksgiving Service of the RCCG, themed “Acceptable Service,” held at the church’s National Headquarters, The Throne of Grace, Ebute-Metta, Lagos. The service also featured prayers for Nigeria, its leaders and citizens. Representing President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the event, Sanwo-Olu acknowledged the role of prayers in nation-building and commended the Christian community, particularly the RCCG, for its continued efforts towards the spiritual and moral development of the country. The governor urged Nigerians to uphold patriotism, resilience and determination, saying national development required collective responsibility. “The Nigeria we want cannot be built by government alone. It requires each of us to play our part, believe in our country, and work together towards a better future,” Sanwo-Olu said. He added, “I encourage every Lagosian to keep pushing forward and doing their part. Progress comes when we work together and keep faith in our state and our country.” Sanwo-Olu said the thanksgiving provided an opportunity for Nigerians to reflect on the country’s past, present and the future they collectively desired to build. He also introduced the APC governorship candidate, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and his running mate to the congregation. In his sermon, Adeboye charged Nigerians, particularly leaders, to understand the essence of true service, stressing that every individual had a purpose and responsibility to fulfil. “We are created for service. If you are alive today, it is because God is giving you a little more time—perhaps so that you may begin to serve,” Adeboye said. He warned against unproductive lives, saying those who claimed to serve God must ensure that their service was driven by the right motives. According to him, service to God becomes acceptable when it is motivated by a genuine desire to do His will and serve humanity. “If you know the will of your Master and do not do it, such a person is living on borrowed time because they are occupying space that could be given to someone else,” he said. Adeboye also cautioned that religious activities, including miracles and other spiritual works, did not automatically make a person’s service acceptable if the motive behind them was wrong. He urged Nigerians to remember the inevitability of divine judgment, saying actions and motives would ultimately be tested. “Let us remember the day of judgment. We can pretend that we are serving God, that we are doing everything He wants us to do for His people, but you cannot deceive God,” he said. Adeboye illustrated his message with the functions of different parts of the human body, saying each was created for a specific purpose. He said the hands, legs, eyes and mouth were designed for productive purposes, while cautioning against using the mouth for gossip and other negative activities. Also at the service was the African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, who called for peace, progress and greater national cohesion. Sowore said Nigerians should appreciate the relative peace in the country and work together across religious lines to promote national development. “It is important that everybody in the country should appreciate the fact that we are still experiencing some kind of peace, but we all really need peace and progress in the country. “We are also ready to work with everybody, whether Muslim or Christian,” he said. The service featured dedicated prayers for Nigeria led by Pastor Foluke Adeboye, wife of the RCCG General Overseer. She prayed for God’s mercy and forgiveness of the nation’s sins, as well as wisdom for leaders and divine intervention in the affairs of the country. items.title: Vols France – Algérie : les billets prennent l’ascenseur pour les vacances de la Toussaint
items.description: Les Algériens de France font face à une nouvelle flambée des prix des billets d'avion à destination de l'Algérie. Cette nouvelle hausse des tarifs intervient à quelques jours des vacances de la Toussaint. Les vacances scolaires de la Toussaint sont prévues du 17 octobre au 2 novembre 2026 en France. Une occasion pour les Algériens de France de visiter leurs proches et leurs familles en Algérie. À moins de deux semaines avant le jour J, les billets d'avion chez les compagnies aériennes desservant l'Algérie au départ de la France ont, sans grande surprise, flambé, dépassant le plafond des 500 € pour certaines routes. Des billets à plus de 500 € chez Air Algérie Si cette flambée confirme encore une fois que les Algériens de France ne ratent pas une occasion de se rendre dans leur pays d'origine avec leurs enfants, elle souligne aussi l'impitoyable logique du principe de l'offre et de la demande qui permet aux compagnies aériennes de se remplir les poches en quelques jours. Chez Air Algérie , le Paris – Alger, en aller-simple, proposé à seulement 140 € pour le 5 octobre, est affiché à plus de 380 € pour le 16 octobre et à plus de 480 € pour le 17 octobre, soit pour le début des vacances de la Toussaint. Cela vaut aussi pour les autres vols de la compagnie aérienne nationale. À titre d'exemple, Air Algérie propose son vol Mulhouse – Constantine à plus de 555 € pour le 17 octobre et son vol Marseille – Oran à plus de 470 € pour la même date. Vols France – Algérie : les billets sont chers, même chez les compagnies à bas coût Chez Transavia, le billet Paris – Alger, affiché à seulement 102 € pour le 5 octobre, est proposé à près de 400 € pour le 17 octobre. La low cost française affiche aussi ses billets pour le vol Nantes – Oran à partir de 313 € pour le 16 octobre. ASL Airlines, qui se présente comme une spécialiste de l'Algérie, ne fait pas exception. La low cost française propose son Paris – Alger en aller-simple à partir de 150 € pour le 5 octobre, avant d’augmenter les tarifs jusqu’à atteindre les 339 € pour le 17 octobre. Enfin, Volotea ne manque pas à l'appel et affiche son billet Bordeaux – Alger à plus de 250 € pour le 16 octobre alors qu’il ne coûte pas plus de 120 € du 5 au 15 octobre. La compagnie à bas coût espagnole propose aussi son vol Marseille – Oran à plus de 400 € du 17 au 20 octobre, alors que le même billet est affiché à 160 € pour le 7 octobre. Les Algériens de France à la merci du principe de l'offre et de la demande En quelques jours seulement, les prix sont montés en flèche. Ils ont triplé, voire quadruplé. Cette flambée annonce clairement que de nombreux Algériens de France ont choisi de passer leurs vacances de la Toussaint dans leur pays d'origine, près de leurs familles et de leurs amis. Cette énième confirmation de la diaspora de son attachement à l'Algérie n’empêche pas toutefois de s'interroger sur les mécanismes que peut adopter l'État pour endiguer les flambées des prix des billets d'avion qui gâchent le voyage des Algériens de France à chaque occasion. L’article Vols France – Algérie : les billets prennent l'ascenseur pour les vacances de la Toussaint est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 10 African countries with the longest coastlines
items.description: African countries are surrounded by the Atlantic and Indian oceans, as well as the Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea, giving dozens of countries access to major maritime routes. Some African countries, however, have significantly longer coastlines than others. Island nations such as Madagascar benefit from their extensive maritime boundaries, while several mainland countries also have coastlines stretching thousands of kilometres. Based on coastline data attributed to the CIA World Factbook, here are the 10 African countries with the longest coastlines: 1. Madagascar — 4,828 km Madagascar has the longest coastline in Africa, stretching approximately 4,828 kilometres. The island nation lies off the southeastern coast of mainland Africa in the Indian Ocean. Its large size and extensive shoreline make it the continent’s leading country by coastline length. 2. Somalia — 3,025 km Somalia has Africa’s second-longest coastline at approximately 3,025 kilometres. Its coastline extends along the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean, giving the country one of the most extensive maritime frontiers on the African mainland. 3. Morocco — 2,945 km Morocco ranks third with approximately 2,945 kilometres of coastline in the CIA-derived dataset. The country’s coastline faces both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. This makes Morocco one of Africa’s most strategically positioned coastal countries. 4. South Africa — 2,798 km South Africa has approximately 2,798 kilometres of coastline. Its coastline stretches from the Atlantic Ocean in the west to the Indian Ocean in the east, giving the country access to two major ocean systems. 5. Mozambique — 2,470 km Mozambique has a coastline of approximately 2,470 kilometres , making it the fifth-longest in Africa. The country’s eastern coastline runs along the Indian Ocean, with numerous bays and islands contributing to its extensive maritime geography. 6. Egypt — 2,450 km Egypt has approximately 2,450 kilometres of coastline. The country has coastlines along both the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, giving it an important position between Europe, Africa and Asia. 7. Eritrea — 2,234 km Eritrea’s coastline stretches for approximately 2,234 kilometres. The country occupies a strategic position along the Red Sea, opposite the Arabian Peninsula, and its coastline includes numerous islands. 8. Libya — 1,770 km Libya has approximately 1,770 kilometres of Mediterranean coastline. Its coastline makes Libya one of the countries with the longest Mediterranean shores in Africa. 9. Angola — 1,600 km Angola has approximately 1,600 kilometres of coastline along the Atlantic Ocean. Its coastal position has historically made the country an important part of Atlantic maritime trade in southern Africa. 10. Namibia — 1,572 km Namibia rounds out the top 10 with approximately 1,572 kilometres of coastline. Its Atlantic coast is dominated by the Namib Desert, creating the distinctive landscape for which the country’s shoreline is known. items.title: Miss Guinée : le COMIGUI élargit l’âge des candidates et renforce son ambition internationale autour du leadership féminin
items.description: Le Comité d’organisation de Miss Guinée (COMIGUI) a lancé, samedi 3 octobre 2026, la quatrième édition du concours Miss Guinée, à l’occasion d’une conférence de presse organisée dans un réceptif hôtelier de Conakry. Cette nouvelle édition est placée sous le thème : « Femmes et Environnement, leadership féminin pour une Guinée durable ». La rencontre a réuni les responsables du comité d’organisation, les représentantes de la Guinée aux compétitions internationales ainsi que plusieurs partenaires. Elle a permis de présenter les grandes lignes de l’édition 2026-2027, mais également les échéances internationales auxquelles les représentantes guinéennes doivent prendre part. La présidente du COMIGUI, Aminata Diallo, a expliqué l’objectif de cette rencontre : « On est ici, c’est pour présenter non seulement nos miss qui doivent partir à l’international, et comme vous le savez, et lancer le début des activités de Miss Guinée, qui vont commencer à partir du 14 à l’intérieur du pays. » Des présélections régionales à partir du 14 octobre Membre du comité d’organisation, Lassine Koné a d’abord remercié les médias pour leur accompagnement depuis le lancement du concours. « Merci d’être venus à cette activité organisée par le comité d’organisation Miss Guinée. C’est un réel plaisir pour nous de vous recevoir également dans ce réceptif hôtelier de la place. Une fois de plus, vous parler du projet Miss Guinée qui d’ailleurs n’est plus à présenter. Puisque on estime que chacun d’entre vous est acteur et partie prenante de ce projet, du début jusqu’à la fin. » Revenant sur les précédentes éditions, il a indiqué que le comité entendait s’appuyer sur les enseignements tirés depuis 2023. « Comme à l’accoutumée, comme les trois précédentes éditions, 2023, 2024 et 2025, nous avons maintenu un peu le même programme d’activités, mais avec plus d’ardeur, avec plus de prise de conscience afin de non seulement essayer de corriger toutes les erreurs du passé, parce qu’il y en a eu, on est conscient de cela. Vous étiez là également à nos côtés, on voit vos critiques, vos suggestions. J’espère que ces critiques, ces suggestions ont été prises en compte à tous les niveaux. » Concernant les candidatures, le comité annonce une ouverture aux jeunes filles et femmes guinéennes âgées de 18 à 35 ans. « Cette année, le programme d’activités 2026-2027 se déroule comme suit : vous avez déjà suivi avec nous l’annonce sur les réseaux sociaux, le volet digital, l’appel à candidature, l’appel à inscription qui est un appel ouvert à toutes les jeunes filles et femmes guinéennes cette année âgées de 18 à 35 ans. En 2023, on était sur 18-25 ans, et cette année c’est ouvert à 18-35 ans, et cet appel a produit ses fruits. Nous avons déjà commencé à enregistrer pas mal de candidatures sur l’ensemble du territoire. » Les présélections régionales débuteront le 14 octobre à N’Zérékoré. « À la suite de cette phase, nous allons entamer les concours de présélection au niveau régional. Comme la présidente l’a mentionné tout à l’heure, la première date à retenir c’est le 14 octobre du côté de N’Zérékoré, nous allons faire la présélection de N’Zérékoré. Ensuite, le 17 octobre 2026, nous serons du côté de Kankan. Le 24 octobre 2026, la région de la Moyenne-Guinée verra à son tour une organisation pour élire justement le trio régional. Et nous allons boucler l’étape des présélections régionales à l’intérieur du pays par la zone exclusive de Boké. Et enfin, nous allons continuer, boucler la dernière activité qui concerne la zone spéciale de Conakry au compte des présélections. » Trois représentantes dans des compétitions internationales La vice-présidente du COMIGUI, Moudatou Bah, a présenté les trois compétitions internationales auxquelles la Guinée participera. Concernant Miss Global, elle a précisé : « La première, il s’agit de Miss Global. Miss Global se tient déjà, ça fait je pense que c’est la 6e ou la 4e journée. Nous avons notre dauphine Fatima Baldé qui est déjà là-bas en Thaïlande et qui a commencé les compétitions, raison pour laquelle elle n’est pas présente ici avec nous aujourd’hui. » Elle a également détaillé les enjeux de cette participation : « Le principal enjeu, c’est le rayonnement de la culture et la représentation internationale de notre pays. Il s’agit de présenter la diversité culturelle de la Guinée, la communication et surtout les projets sociaux. » Pour Miss Univers, prévue en novembre à Porto Rico, la Guinée sera représentée par Justine Camara. « La deuxième compétition internationale à laquelle nous allons participer, c’est Miss Univers. Donc Miss Univers se tiendra en novembre et ce sera à Porto Rico. Notre pays sera représenté par madame Justine Camara, qui est là aujourd’hui. » Selon Moudatou Bah, les critères seront notamment liés au charisme et à la capacité de représentation. « Ce qui compte le plus, c’est le charisme, la prise de parole, la présence scénique, l’engagement et l’image internationale. » Enfin, Matoma Condé, Miss Guinée 2026, représentera le pays à Miss Cosmos, prévu en décembre au Vietnam. « La troisième compétition, c’est Miss Cosmos. Donc qui va se dérouler en décembre au Viêt Nam. Et à cette compétition, notre pays sera représenté par mademoiselle Matoma Condé qui est présente aujourd’hui, donc Miss nationale, Miss Guinée, qui est notre Miss actuelle. Donc là c’est la beauté, l’intelligence, la créativité, la communication et les projets à portée internationale. » Représentante de la Guinée à Miss Univers, Justine Camara a exprimé sa détermination à porter les couleurs nationales à Porto Rico. «Je suis très heureuse d’être avec vous aujourd’hui. Pour ceux qui ne me connaissent pas, donc je suis une femme franco-guinéenne, et je porte aujourd’hui fièrement l’écharpe de Miss Guinée Univers. J’ai cette responsabilité en novembre prochain à Porto Rico de représenter dignement la Guinée. » Elle entend notamment promouvoir l’image du pays et mettre en avant les femmes guinéennes. «Ça me tient à cœur de faire rayonner la Guinée à l’international, de montrer la beauté de la Guinée, de montrer ses paysages, de promouvoir aussi ses femmes. » La candidate souhaite également mettre l’accent sur la jeunesse. «J’ai aussi l’honneur de représenter, en tout cas j’espère, de mettre un accent sur la jeunesse guinéenne. C’est d’ailleurs pour ça que j’ai créé cette association pour contribuer au bien-être des enfants défavorisés et fragilisés en Guinée, ce que je commence déjà à faire à travers plusieurs missions. » Sur ses origines, Justine Camara a ajouté : « Il faut savoir que mon papa est Guinéen, il vient de la Guinée forestière, il a grandi et il est né à N’Zérékoré. Il m’a transmis toutes les valeurs guinéennes, toute son histoire guinéenne, tous ses souvenirs. Ça fait maintenant presque 10 ans que je viens en Guinée chaque année. » Elle assure poursuivre activement sa préparation : «Je me prépare énormément depuis plusieurs mois, que ce soit sur l’aspect physique, que ce soit aussi sur l’aspect oratoire. Il faut savoir que l’anglais prime beaucoup. Même si je parle anglais, je continue à prendre des cours pour pratiquer. C’est pas Justine Camara qui me soutient, mais c’est toute la Guinée qu’on veut voir briller à l’international. Depuis mon sacre, j’ai travaillé sur mon projet sur la création d’une ONG Femmes Créatrices de Guinée et par la même occasion, j’ai continué à me préparer sur plusieurs aspects pour la compétition internationale, qui s’est avérée être Miss Cosmos. À ce niveau, je me suis préparée sur mon aspect physique et intellectuel, et aussi sur la communication. Et je continue toujours à me préparer sur l’aspect culturel.» La candidate insiste également sur l’importance d’un accompagnement financier.«Je continue aussi à déposer des demandes de sponsoring parce qu’il est vraiment important que je sois accompagnée financièrement, pas seulement que physiquement, que je sois accompagnée financièrement. » Pour Matoma Condé, sa participation dépasse sa propre personne. «Si je vais à Miss Cosmos, c’est pas seulement Matoma Condé qui va à Miss Cosmos, c’est toute la Guinée. Donc je demande à tout un chacun de me soutenir, de liker et de continuer aussi à me soutenir comme il le faut, parce que c’est la Guinée qui va à Miss Cosmos et non Matoma Condé. » Avec cette quatrième édition, le COMIGUI entend ainsi poursuivre l’organisation du concours national tout en renforçant la présence de la Guinée sur la scène internationale. Placée sous le thème du leadership féminin et de l’environnement, cette édition met également en avant les initiatives, l’engagement et la représentation des femmes guinéennes.
