items.title: We will empower the grassroots and protect every vote – NPP’s 1st Vice Chair Kojo Bamba
items.description: Newly elected National First Vice Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Kwadwo Fosu Boadu, popularly known as Kojo Bamba, has pledged to prioritise the grassroots and protect the party’s votes as the NPP begins preparations for the 2028 general election. In a message posted on Facebook after his election on Sunday, October 4, after his elections, Mr Boadu said strengthening the party at the grassroots would be a key priority as the party prepares for 2028. He said the grassroots would need to be empowered to play an effective role in the party’s activities, while measures would also be taken to protect the party’s votes throughout the electoral process. “The journey to 2028 starts now. We will empower the grassroots. We will protect every vote. We will work as one family,” he said. “Together, we can win!” he added. Mr Boadu expressed gratitude to delegates for electing him and said he was deeply humbled by the confidence they had placed in him. “I am deeply humbled and grateful to the delegates of the New Patriotic Party for the confidence reposed in me as the newly elected National 1st Vice Chairman,” he said. Read also: From Delta Force to NPP First Vice Chairman – Kojo Bamba’s political journey Mr Boadu said his victory should not be seen as a personal achievement, but as a victory for the party’s grassroots members, constituency executives, youth and women’s organisers, and delegates who supported his vision. “This victory is not mine alone. It belongs to every grassroots foot soldier, every constituency executive, every youth and women’s organiser, and every delegate who believed in the vision of protecting our ballot boxes from the polling station to the collation centres,” he said. He pledged to take up the responsibility with humility and a commitment to serving the party, while working with the new national leadership to strengthen the NPP. “I accept this responsibility with humility and a firm commitment to serve,” he said. Mr Boadu said he would work with the newly elected National Chairman, John Boadu, and the rest of the national executive to rebuild and unite the party ahead of the next general election. “Together with our new National Chairman, John Boadu, and the entire national executive, we will work tirelessly to rebuild, unite, and strengthen our great party,” he said. Mr Boadu, who rose from the party’s grassroots to become one of its national executives, secured 3,116 votes to emerge first among 13 candidates contesting the three Vice Chairmanship positions at the NPP’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3. From Delta Force to NPP leadership Mr Boadu’s political journey began at the grassroots and included a controversial period as leader of Delta Force, a pro-NPP vigilante group that gained notoriety in the Ashanti Region after the party’s 2016 electoral victory. A former auto mechanic, he led the group during a period of heightened political tension, including opposition to the appointment of George Adjei as Ashanti Regional Security Coordinator. Read Also: From Delta Force to NPP First Vice Chairman – Kojo Bamba’s political journey In 2018, Mr Boadu was appointed Deputy National Director of Operations of the NPP’s youth wing, marking his transition into the party’s formal structures. During his campaign for the First Vice Chairmanship, he placed particular emphasis on grassroots mobilisation and the welfare of constituency executives, describing them as the party’s frontline workers. His election now places him among the NPP’s national leadership as the party prepares for the 2028 general election. He will serve alongside newly elected National Chairman John Boadu, Second Vice Chairman Henry Nana Boakye and Third Vice Chairman Nana Akomea. Mr Boadu ended his message by stressing the broader purpose of his new role: “The NPP must rise again in 2028, not just for political power, but for the countless dreams and destinies that depend on a brighter future.”

items.title: 2027: ADC accuses APC of threatening voters with AK-47
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC PCC, has accused the All Progressives Congress, APC, of threatening Nigerians with violence ahead of the 2027 presidential election over an alleged AK-47 threat by the party’s Edo State chairman, Jarrett Tenebe. The council said the alleged threat, coupled with a reported attack on ADC members and destruction of their vehicles in Gegu, Koton Karfi Local Government Area of Kogi State, showed the need for urgent action to prevent intimidation and violence ahead of the election. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, on Sunday, the ADC PCC demanded that the police, Department of State Services, DSS, and Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, investigate Tenebe over the alleged threat. Ologbondiyan said the council had waited for the APC leadership and President Bola Tinubu to condemn or demand a retraction of the alleged statement but received no such response. “We are shocked that a state chairman of a ruling party, Mr. Jarrett Tenebe, can stand before the public and threaten Nigerians with AK-47 rifles if they refuse to vote for his party, the APC,” he said. He urged the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS Director-General and INEC to invite Tenebe for questioning, arguing that the alleged threat violated the Electoral Act and the Constitution. Ologbondiyan also challenged the APC’s claim of securing 2.5 million votes in Edo State for Tinubu in 2027, saying such a figure could not be achieved through a free, fair and credible election. He attributed the alleged threat to growing political desperation within the ruling party, citing what he described as increasing hardship, insecurity and dissatisfaction among Edo voters. According to him, the alleged statement had reinforced concerns that the APC might resort to violence and intimidation in its bid to retain power in 2027. The ADC PCC also appealed to the United Nations, European Union, African Union, ECOWAS, United States and other democratic countries to monitor developments ahead of the election and prevail on the Federal Government and APC to ensure a peaceful and credible electoral process. Ologbondiyan said the 2027 election would be ‘a referendum’ on the performance of the APC-led administration, insisting that intimidation would not stop Nigerians from exercising their constitutional right to vote. The council also called for investigation into the reported attack on ADC members and destruction of vehicles belonging to supporters in Gegu, Koton Karfi. “We call on the members of our Kogi State chapter, particularly in Koton Karfi Local Government, to name everyone they identified in the course of the needless attack,” he said. Ologbondiyan urged security agencies to thoroughly investigate the incident and prosecute anyone found culpable. items.title: 2027: Kano APC chieftain urges unity, dialogue
items.description: …Appeals to Tinubu, Yari to reconcile party leaders By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kano State, Aminu Shehu Uba Sharada, has appealed to President Bola Tinubu and the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Senator Abdulaziz Yari, to urgently intervene in what he described as disagreements among party leaders and stakeholders in the state. Sharada, who is Personal Assistant to Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, made the appeal in a statement on Sunday, saying the differences within the Kano APC needed to be addressed to prevent possible consequences for the party in the 2027 elections. He urged the national leadership to initiate consultations, reconciliation and genuine political engagement with relevant stakeholders in the state. Sharada said, “Let me be frank: anyone giving the impression that everything is fine within the Kano APC is not giving the President the full picture. “There are disagreements and visible concerns among party leaders and stakeholders, and if they are not addressed early, they could have wider consequences for the party.” According to him, there was no justification for the continued disagreements and confrontations within the party, arguing that the challenges ahead were bigger than individual interests. “At this point, I believe there is no justification for the continued disagreements, confrontations and arguments within our party in Kano State. The challenges before us are bigger than individual interests, and the only way forward is for our leaders and stakeholders to come together and resolve their differences in the interest of the party,” he said. Sharada said the APC’s immediate responsibility should be to build a united party capable of securing electoral victories at the presidential, governorship, senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly levels. He therefore appealed to Tinubu and Yari to pay particular attention to the situation in the Kano chapter and facilitate what he described as a timely intervention. “This is not the time to take sides or deepen existing divisions. It is time for consultation, reconciliation and genuine political engagement. “Every leader and stakeholder has a role to play in bringing the various interests together and rebuilding confidence within the party,” he said. Sharada said the APC had a broad base of committed members and stakeholders in Kano, adding that what was needed was leadership capable of bringing the various interests together, listening to their concerns and establishing a common direction. He urged the national and state leadership of the party to act swiftly and place the interests of the APC above personal disagreements. “There is still time to resolve our differences. What is required now is the political will, sincerity and leadership to do so,” he said. The post 2027: Kano APC chieftain urges unity, dialogue appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Wike presses Amaechi on $308m power plants proceeds
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Federal Capital Territory FCT minister, Nyesom Wike, has pressed a former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi, to account for the $308 million proceeds from the sale of the state’s power plants during his administration. Wike spoke on Sunday at a town hall meeting with leaders, elders and stakeholders of the Ogbakor Etche in Etche Local Government Area of Rivers State. “Amaechi sold the gas turbine power stations for $308 million. Where is the money? What did Rivers people get from it? So, where is the money? Rivers people are asking: what happened to the $308 million?”, he asked. The minister accused his predecessor of failing to turn his eight years as governor, from 2007 to 2015, and eight years as Minister of Transportation into development and opportunities for Rivers people. “When you had the opportunity to be governor of Rivers State, what did you bring to our people? From Igwuruta to Chokochoko, it was a problem. From Chokochoko to Omoku, it was a problem. “You became Minister of Transportation for eight years. Which person from our area did you bring to the limelight? Mention just one!”, he challenged Amaechi. Wike urged the people of Etche to reject politicians whose main concern, he said, was political survival rather than the development of their communities. He said support should be based on tangible achievements and opportunities delivered to the people. He cited what he described as concrete gains for the area, among them the appointment of Professor Dimiri Mercury as Vice-Chancellor of Rivers State University and the establishment of the university’s Faculty of Agriculture campus there. He also listed the political appointments of Senator Allwell Onyesoh and House of Representatives member Kelechi Wogu as benefits of political engagement and alliances. He said; “Politics is not about what one person will gain. Politics is about what your people will gain. Ask yourself; what has this person brought to our people? What has he done to improve the lives of our people? What opportunities have been created? We must begin to ask these questions because politics without development is meaningless.” Wike told the gathering that the people of the region must “wise up” politically and decide on the basis of what would advance their communities. He said allegiance should no longer be built around individuals but around programmes, development and opportunities. Earlier, Wike and other political stakeholders paid a condolence visit to the palace of the late Etche/Ochie of Etche land, Emmanuel Opurum, a member of the Rivers State council of traditional rulers who died at the age of 106. The minister pledged to support the family in the burial arrangements. He also praised the administration of President Bola Tinubu, saying its emphasis on due process, accountability and development offered a new direction for governance. He urged the people to align with the President’s development-oriented agenda rather than back politicians out of personal loyalty. “Under the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu, we are witnessing a system that respects the rule of law and demands absolute transparency from public office holders, Governance is about lifting the people, not about personal aggrandisement or evading lawful inquiries into state properties. When people loot or mismanage the commonwealth, the law must take its course”, Wike said. The post Wike presses Amaechi on $308m power plants proceeds appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Britain's Green Party votes to class Zionism as a form of racism
items.description: By David Milliken LONDON, Oct 4 (Reuters) - Britain's Green Party voted on Sunday to class Zionism as a form of racism, drawing criticism from British Jews and from the Israeli government which said it now viewed the party as "a body that gives legitimacy to terrorism". The party – which received 6% of the vote in national elections in 2024 – said it regarded Zionism as "an ethnonationalist political project" and repeated its call for Britain's Labour government to end all arms trade with Israel.

items.title: Iran's oil minister resigns, no reason given
items.description: DUBAI, Oct 4 (Reuters) - Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned and Hamid Bovard, chief executive of the government-owned National Iranian Oil Company, will be in charge of the ministry as acting minister, state media said on Sunday, without providing a reason for the resignation. Mohsen Paknejad has been the oil minister of the OPEC member country since August 2024 and resigns as the seven-month war between Iran and the US puts pressure on the country's economy.

items.title: Nwifuru hails Ishiagu community for sustained peace
items.description: …As community honours governor, Anyim, Umahi, Osi, others By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has commended the people of Ishiagu community in Ivo Local Government Area for sustaining peace and unity despite longstanding interests in the area’s mineral resources. Nwifuru also commended former Senate President and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator Anyim Pius Anyim, for his efforts towards promoting unity in the community. The governor, who was represented by his Deputy, Mrs Patricia Obila, spoke during the Ishiagu Day and Hall of Fame celebration organised by the community. He expressed appreciation to the people for honouring him and endorsing his administration for a second term in the 2027 governorship election. Nwifuru assured the community that his second term, if secured, would bring greater democratic dividends and increased infrastructural investment to Ishiagu. The community honoured Nwifuru, Anyim, Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, Chief Gideon Osi and other prominent indigenes and stakeholders with awards for their contributions to the development of Ebonyi State and Nigeria. Speaking at the event, Anyim commended Nwifuru for his efforts towards restoring peace in Ishiagu and executing projects aimed at improving the welfare of residents. He described the award as a testament to the community’s appreciation of the governor’s commitment, urging residents to sustain the peace and cooperation that had enabled them to come together for the celebration. The Chairman of Ivo Local Government Area, Chief Stanley Anyim, also hailed the return of peace to the community, saying it made the event possible. “I have seen that peace has come to stay in Ivo Local Government, and that is why they were able to organise this type of programme. “If it was before, this could not happen, but today, Ishiagu people have been relieved of everyday trouble. “I will make sure I uphold this peace and the programme. I want the people to maintain peace,” he said. One of the award recipients, Chief Gideon Osi, described his recognition as a testimony to his years of service to humanity. Osi cited medical outreaches, scholarships, skills training and assistance to residents among his interventions in the community. He said the Hall of Fame should go beyond celebrating individuals and serve as an inspiration for residents to contribute to the development of their community. Osi urged successful members of the community to use their resources to support others rather than intimidate them. He also called for caution in disputes involving land and mineral resources, stressing that Ishiagu’s mineral wealth could provide long-term benefits to the people if properly harnessed. A community stakeholder, Oka Franklin, described the event as historic, saying it celebrated the existence, unity, culture and traditions of the Ishiagu people. Franklin expressed hope that the initiative would encourage other communities in Ebonyi State and the South-East to embrace peaceful coexistence. The Chairman of the Central Planning Committee of the event, Bar. Uchenna Orji, said the celebration was organised to recognise excellence in leadership, service and hard work. Orji, a former Commissioner for Information and State Orientation in Ebonyi State, commended the honourees for their contributions to peace and development in the state and urged them to sustain their efforts. He expressed satisfaction with the unity and peace prevailing in Ishiagu and Ebonyi State generally. The post Nwifuru hails Ishiagu community for sustained peace appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Rentrée scolaire : l’intersyndicale appelle les enseignants à reprendre les cours
items.description: À quelques heures de la rentrée scolaire prévue ce lundi 5 octobre 2026, l’intersyndicale de l’éducation appelle les enseignants à reprendre normalement les cours sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Le secrétaire général du Syndicat national de l’éducation (SNE), Michel Pépé Balamou, a donné cette consigne ce dimanche 4 octobre, lors d’une rencontre avec la presse au siège du syndicat, à Matoto. S’exprimant au nom de l’intersyndicale composée de la FSPE, du SLECG et du SNE, élargie au Syndicat national de l’enseignement franco-arabe de Guinée (SNEFAG), il a également annoncé la poursuite des négociations avec le gouvernement. Pas de préavis de grève Michel Pépé Balamou a d’abord tenu à clarifier la position de l’intersyndicale. Il affirme qu’aucun mouvement de grève n’est actuellement engagé dans le secteur de l’éducation. « L’intersyndicale de l’éducation rappelle aux enseignantes et enseignants de Guinée qu’elle n’est pas porteuse d’une plateforme de revendications, ni d’un préavis de grève, à plus forte raison d’un avis de grève. Elle a fait usage de menace. Et comme dans nos jargons syndicaux on a coutume de le dire, la menace porte plus que la grève. Et cette menace à date, a porté, d’autant plus que le gouvernement est sorti de sa zone de confort pour nous recevoir et travailler. » Selon lui, un comité de suivi est désormais chargé de veiller à l’application des engagements pris dans le protocole d’accord signé le 3 janvier 2026. « Au jour d’aujourd’hui, il y a un comité de suivi sous la présidence de Dr Alia Camara, président du Conseil National du Dialogue Social, qui veille à l’application des différentes résolutions issues du protocole d’accord en date du samedi 3 janvier 2026. » Les enseignants invités à reprendre les cours Pour cette rentrée, l’intersyndicale demande donc aux enseignants de reprendre leurs activités, pendant que les négociations avec les autorités se poursuivent. « Par conséquent, nous demandons aux enseignantes et enseignants de Guinée de continuer à dérouler leurs activités didactiques, pédagogiques et académiques sur toute l’étendue du territoire national, le temps pour l’intersyndicale de l’éducation FSPE, SLECG, SNE, de continuer les négociations le lundi interrompues du fait de l’organisation du 68e anniversaire de l’accession à l’indépendance et à la souveraineté nationale de notre pays, une organisation supérieure au-dessus de nos intérêts personnels et collectifs. » Contractuels non retenus : appel à faire confiance à l’intersyndicale La situation des enseignants contractuels non retenus après l’évaluation en pratique de classe, ainsi que celle des enseignants concernés par la jauge spéciale de Conakry, a également été évoquée. Michel Pépé Balamou les invite à faire confiance aux organisations syndicales, qui entendent poursuivre les discussions avec le gouvernement. « Aux enseignants contractuels non retenus à l’issue de l’évaluation en pratique de classe et ceux de la jauge spéciale du Conakry, invite leur est faite, de faire confiance à l’intersyndicale de l’éducation FSPE, SLECG, SNE, élargie au SNEFAG, afin de trouver dans un bref délai des voies et issues conformes à l’esprit et à la lettre du point 7 du protocole d’accord bipartite gouvernement – intersyndicale de l’éducation en date du samedi 3 janvier 2026. » L’intersyndicale maintient la pression Si elle privilégie pour l’heure le dialogue, l’intersyndicale n’entend pas pour autant abandonner ses revendications. Elle demande au gouvernement de respecter les engagements contenus dans le protocole d’accord du 3 janvier 2026. « Par voie de conséquence, l’intersyndicale de l’éducation FSPE, SLECG, SNE élargie au SNEFAG invite le gouvernement à faire du dialogue social un mode de gouvernance et de stabilisation des relations du travail en respectant scrupuleusement tous les engagements pris dans le protocole d’accord du 3 janvier 2026, et à comprendre que l’intersyndicale de l’éducation a une arme fatale qu’elle pourrait utiliser en début, en milieu et enfin d’année scolaire comme elle a su le faire le 1er décembre 2025. » Le secrétaire général du SNE insiste enfin sur le fait que l’apaisement recherché à l’occasion de la rentrée ne constitue pas un renoncement aux revendications syndicales. « Cette opportunité d’apaisement, de compréhension n’est pas une faiblesse, ni un recul, encore moins une conception de parfum de corruption ou d’achat de conscience, loin s’en faut. L’intersyndicale de l’éducation fait une saine appréciation des réalités du moment, mais tout en tenant compte des intérêts matériels et moraux de ses militants, et invite sa base militante à rester vigilante, mobilisée pour répondre à un éventuel appel par des moyens légaux afin de faire aboutir tous ces points de revendication contenus dans le protocole d’accord bipartite gouvernement – intersyndicale de l’éducation FSPE, SNE, SLECG en date du samedi 3 janvier 2026. » Ainsi, pour cette rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, l’intersyndicale privilégie la reprise des cours et la poursuite du dialogue avec le gouvernement, tout en maintenant sa mobilisation autour des engagements pris en janvier dernier. items.title: Makinde to Tinubu: Rescue abducted NYSC members now
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement, APM, Seyi Makinde, has challenged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to urgently rescue the prospective National Youth Service Corps members abducted in Imo State on Independence Day, saying every hour they remain in captivity is one hour too long. Four days after the abduction, the corps members are still in captivity, with Makinde demanding that the Federal Government move decisively to secure their release and that of other Nigerians held by abductors across the country. In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communications of Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, Richard Ihediwa, Makinde also demanded the unconditional release and safe return of Nigerians abducted in Niger, Kwara, Kaduna, Zamfara, Sokoto, Katsina, Borno and other parts of the country. “One hour in captivity is one hour too long, and one victim in captivity is one victim too many,” Makinde said. He said the government could not afford to overlook the security and wellbeing of citizens, citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which places the security and welfare of citizens among the primary purposes of government. Makinde further argued that the Federal Government bears a particular responsibility for the safety of youths once they are called up for the NYSC programme. He said insecurity could no longer be treated with rhetoric, lip service or kid gloves, accusing the All Progressives Congress, APC, administration of failing to confront the crisis decisively. The APM presidential candidate alleged that terrorist elements had killed more than 600,000 Nigerians in the last three and a half years, with countless others still in captivity. “These ugly indices are unacceptable and can no longer be overlooked by Nigerians,” Makinde said. He said Nigerians were determined to vote out the Tinubu administration in 2027 over what he described as its failure in office, but maintained that the political contest could not absolve the government of its immediate duty to protect citizens. Makinde called on Tinubu to act now, deal decisively with insecurity and bring back the abducted corps members and other Nigerians languishing in the hands of their abductors. The post Makinde to Tinubu: Rescue abducted NYSC members now appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La Policía empieza a desalojar el asentamiento de migrantes de la playa de El Trampolín de Ceuta
items.description: La Policía Nacional ha desalojado parcialmente el asentamiento de migrantes de la playa de El Trampolín , en Ceuta, con un imponente operativo desplegado este domingo. Tras una noche sin presencia policial, sobre las 7.30 ha llegado la primera furgoneta de la Unidad de Intervención Policial (UIP) para una toma de contacto inicial. Aún no había amanecido, la bruma cubría el mar y la mayoría de migrantes seguían durmiendo. Minutos después, un dron ha empezado a sobrevolar la zona y, finalmente, el amplio dispositivo ha arrancado por sorpresa ya a las 8.00. A esa hora, medio centenar de furgonetas de la Policía Nacional, tres tanquetas de los antidisturbios y otra decena de vehículos pesados del Ejército han irrumpido entre la neblina, todos de golpe, para perimetrar los accesos y dividir el poblado en varios sectores. A las 19.00, los agentes seguían llevándose a grupos de gente. Varios han intentado escapar por el agua. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Flamme des JOJ Dakar 2026 : Ndar vibre au rythme de la Flamme des JOJ
items.description: La ville tricentenaire a vibré samedi 3 octobre au rythme de la Flamme des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026. Portée sur les eaux du fleuve Sénégal par deux enfants de la Langue de Barbarie, Fary Seye et Ousseynou Diop, elle a traversé une cité en fête, entre chants, danses, tambours et animations culturelles. Saint-Louis a vécu, samedi 3 et dimanche 4 octobre, un moment fort avec l’arrivée de la Flamme des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Dans les rues comme sur les berges du fleuve Sénégal, les populations se sont mobilisées pour accueillir ce symbole olympique, dans une ambiance festive et populaire. Le passage de la Flamme a été marqué par une séquence spectaculaire sur le fleuve. Portée sur les eaux, elle a offert aux Saint-Louisiens un moment à la fois solennel et festif. Deux enfants de la Langue de Barbarie ont été choisis pour porter la Flamme : Fary Seye, ancienne championne du Sénégal et d’Afrique de judo, aujourd’hui arbitre internationale, et Ousseynou Diop, champion de la traversée Dakar-Gorée à la nage. Tout au long du parcours, Saint-Louis a dévoilé son patrimoine culturel. Les chants et danses de la troupe de Fanal, les prestations des faux lions et les rythmes des tambours-majors ont contribué à installer une atmosphère particulièrement chaleureuse. La mascotte officielle des JOJ, Ayo, a également été accueillie sous les acclamations du public. Présent à Saint-Louis, Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, président du Comité national olympique et sportif sénégalais (CNOSS) et du Comité d’organisation des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (COJOJ), a pris part à cette mobilisation en compagnie d’autres officiels. Pour Alioune Badara Diop, adjoint au maire de Saint-Louis, cette étape illustre les valeurs communes entre la ville et l’olympisme, notamment la paix, la solidarité et la fraternité. Le passage de la Flamme a coïncidé avec la troisième édition des CyberGames, consacrée à la cybersécurité et à l’innovation. Compétitions de « Capture The Flag », démonstrations et échanges autour du numérique ont permis de placer la jeunesse au cœur de l’événement. Entre sport, culture, innovation et mobilisation populaire, Saint-Louis a ainsi offert au Flame Tour une étape haute en couleurs, faisant de ses rues et de ses berges un véritable espace de célébration des valeurs olympiques. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: Top 10 African countries with the most fighter jets in 2026
items.description: Air power remains an important part of military capability across Africa, with several countries maintaining sizeable fleets of fighter and interceptor aircraft. According to Global Firepower’s 2026 Fighter Fleet Strength ranking, Egypt has the largest fighter/interceptor fleet in Africa, followed by Algeria and Morocco. Global Firepower describes the category as fighter/interceptor aircraft and includes platforms such as the F-16, F-15, F/A-18, Su-27/35, MiG-29, Rafale and Gripen. Its figures are based on aircraft inventory data through 2026. Here are the 10 African countries with the largest fighter/interceptor fleets in 2026: 1. Egypt — 242 Egypt has by far the largest fighter/interceptor fleet in Africa, with 242 aircraft, according to Global Firepower. The country ranks 10th globally in this category. Its air fleet includes fighter platforms such as the F-16, while Egypt also operates Rafale and MiG-29 aircraft. Global Firepower separately lists Egypt with 90 dedicated attack aircraft, meaning those are not included in the 242 fighter figure. 2. Algeria — 111 Algeria ranks second in Africa with 111 fighter/interceptor aircraft. Global Firepower places Algeria 20th globally in the category. Its overall military aircraft inventory is considerably larger because it also operates attack aircraft, transport planes, trainers and helicopters. 3. Morocco — 84 Morocco has 84 fighter/interceptor aircraft, making it the third-largest fleet in Africa. Global Firepower ranks the Moroccan fighter fleet 25th globally. Its wider military aviation inventory also includes 31 transport aircraft, 77 trainers and 73 helicopters. 4. Angola — 67 Angola ranks fourth on the continent with 67 fighter/interceptor aircraft. The country has a substantial military aviation capability, although its fleet includes several different categories of aircraft beyond fighters, including trainers, transport aircraft and helicopters. 5. Sudan — 37 Sudan has 37 fighter/interceptor aircraft, according to the 2026 Global Firepower data. The figure places Sudan ahead of several African countries with established air forces, although its overall military aviation inventory includes other aircraft categories as well. 6. Ethiopia — 25 Ethiopia ranks sixth in Africa with 25 fighter/interceptor aircraft. The country also has a separate fleet of training aircraft and helicopters, meaning the 25 figure should not be interpreted as its total military aircraft inventory. 7. Kenya — 17 Kenya has 17 fighter/interceptor aircraft, placing it seventh among African countries in Global Firepower’s 2026 ranking. 8. Nigeria — 14 Nigeria ranks eighth in Africa with 14 fighter/interceptor aircraft. 9. Namibia — 11 Namibia is tied for ninth with 11 fighter/interceptor aircraft in Global Firepower’s 2026 dataset. 10. Tanzania — 11 Tanzania also has 11 fighter/interceptor aircraft, putting it level with Namibia for the final position in the top 10. items.title: I do not see myself as better than anyone – NPP’s 1st Vice Chair Kojo Bamba
items.description: Newly elected First Vice Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Kwadwo Fosu Boadu, popularly known as Kojo Bamba, says his new position is not about personal advancement but about representing the aspirations of Ghana’s youth. Mr Boadu, who rose from the party’s grassroots to become one of its national executives, secured 3,116 votes to emerge first among 13 candidates contesting the three Vice Chairmanship positions at the NPP’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3. In a message posted on Facebook after his election, Mr Boadu said he did not consider himself superior to the other contenders, describing his role as one of service to young people and the wider party. “I do not see myself as better than anyone else. I see myself as a voice for the youth, a representative of their hopes, dreams and aspirations,” he said. He said his ambition extended beyond personal success, with a focus on creating opportunities for the next generation. “My ambition goes beyond personal success; it is about creating opportunities and ensuring that the next generation has a fair chance to rise.” Mr Boadu said the NPP’s return to power in 2028 was important not only for the party but also for young people whose aspirations, he argued, depended on improved opportunities. “So many destinies risk remaining in the shadows if we fail to restore power in 2028. Our youth deserve opportunities, our people deserve hope, and our future deserves a renewed commitment to progress.” From Delta Force to NPP leadership Mr Boadu’s political journey began at the grassroots and included a controversial period as leader of Delta Force, a pro-NPP vigilante group that gained notoriety in the Ashanti Region after the party’s 2016 electoral victory. A former auto mechanic, he led the group during a period of heightened political tension, including opposition to the appointment of George Adjei as Ashanti Regional Security Coordinator. Read Also: From Delta Force to NPP First Vice Chairman – Kojo Bamba’s political journey In 2018, Mr Boadu was appointed Deputy National Director of Operations of the NPP’s youth wing, marking his transition into the party’s formal structures. During his campaign for the First Vice Chairmanship, he placed particular emphasis on grassroots mobilisation and the welfare of constituency executives, describing them as the party’s frontline workers. His election now places him among the NPP’s national leadership as the party prepares for the 2028 general election. He will serve alongside newly elected National Chairman John Boadu, Second Vice Chairman Henry Nana Boakye and Third Vice Chairman Nana Akomea. Mr Boadu ended his message by stressing the broader purpose of his new role: “The NPP must rise again in 2028, not just for political power, but for the countless dreams and destinies that depend on a brighter future.”

items.title: Shettima’s ‘Caracas’ claim indicts APC, Buhari — ADC campaign
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADCPCC) has said Vice President Kashim Shettima’s claim that President Bola Tinubu saved Nigeria from economic collapse amounts to an indictment of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. The council said if Nigeria was heading towards ‘Caracas’ before Tinubu assumed office, the APC must accept responsibility, having controlled the Federal Government for eight years under Buhari. The position was contained in a statement by the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, on Sunday. Ologbondiyan said the APC could not disown its record under Buhari while Tinubu, who is seeking a second term on its platform, had repeatedly defended the former administration and promised to build on its legacy. “Vice President Shettima’s statement is self-indicting. If Nigeria was heading to Caracas under Buhari, it means Buhari and the APC deceived Nigerians for eight years,” he said. Ologbondiyan said Nigerians were less concerned about political narratives than food and basic necessities, citing deteriorating roads, electricity, public institutions and the rising cost of living. “But Nigerians do not know Buhari as an individual; Nigerians know APC. It is the APC, on whose platform President Tinubu is seeking a second term, that has failed Nigerians for almost 12 years and is undeserving of another four years,” he said. Rejecting Shettima’s description of Nigeria as merely heading towards a ‘Caracas’ scenario, he said Nigerians were already experiencing it. “Nigerians are not heading to Caracas; under the APC, Nigerians are already living the Caracas experience in their own country,” Ologbondiyan said. He also accused the Tinubu administration of worsening hunger, inflation, naira devaluation, insecurity, unemployment and the cost of living. “President Tinubu has not saved Nigeria from collapse; he has pushed the country deeper into economic ruin,” he said. The ADC council also faulted Shettima’s promise to deploy 10,600 electric tricycles, 300 buses and electric taxis under an e-logistics programme, recalling the administration’s earlier promise that transportation costs would fall by October 1, 2026. It urged the APC to acknowledge the challenges facing Nigerians, saying the ADC remained committed to providing an alternative government. items.title: NANS targets 10m students for 2027 elections
items.description: …Sets up nationwide mobilisation committee By Adeola Badru The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has set a target of mobilising at least 10 million Nigerian students to participate in the 2027 general elections. The association also constituted a National Election Mobilisation Committee to coordinate voter sensitisation, mobilisation and monitoring of students’ participation in election-related activities across the country. The move comes as preparations for the 2027 elections intensify, with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) scheduled to hold the presidential and National Assembly elections on February 20, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on March 6, 2027. In a statement signed by its National President, Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, NANS described students as a significant constituency in Nigeria’s democratic process, claiming a membership base of more than 40.1 million students. The association said the size of the student population meant that students could not afford to remain indifferent to the electoral process, particularly because government policies and decisions directly affect them. NANS said, “As the apex student representative body with over 40.1 million Nigerian students as members, we constitute a significant voting bloc in the country.” It added: “It is noteworthy that we are major stakeholders in nation-building, as students constitute a significant segment of the country’s population and are directly affected by government policies and decisions. Hence, we cannot afford to toe the path of apathy or remain indifferent to the democratic process.” According to the association, the mobilisation drive is aimed at promoting informed and responsible participation rather than political apathy among students. “As a body of intellectuals and future leaders, we strongly believe that one of the most important ways citizens can contribute to the democratic process is through informed and active participation in elections. “Therefore, our firm resolve is to encourage Nigerian students to participate actively and responsibly in the forthcoming 2027 General Elections,” NANS said. The association said the newly constituted National Election Mobilisation Committee would coordinate sensitisation, mobilisation and monitoring of students’ participation and election-related activities across the six geopolitical zones. Under the structure, the NANS President will serve as Director-General, while the NANS Senate President will serve as Deputy Director. Olusola Oladoja was appointed National Coordinator, Gambo Abubakar as National Deputy Coordinator, and Charles Obina Ebube as National Public Relations Officer. Agbabiaka Ahmed was named Chairman of the Advisory Committee for the South, while Ibrahim G. Ibrahim Babalolo will chair the Northern Advisory Committee. The committee has also been decentralised across the six geopolitical zones, with representatives appointed in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. The North-West structure covers Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara and Jigawa states, while the North-East structure covers Borno, Yobe, Taraba, Gombe, Adamawa and Bauchi states. The North-Central structure includes Kwara, Benue, Plateau, Nasarawa, the FCT, Kogi and Niger states. In the South-West, the committee covers Osun, Oyo, Ogun, Lagos, Ekiti and Ondo states, while Bayelsa, Delta, Edo, Cross River, Akwa Ibom and Rivers states make up the South-South zone. The South-East structure covers Imo, Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi and Enugu states. NANS said the committee would commence “immediate sensitisation, mobilisation and monitoring” of students across campuses and institutions. It directed the committee to coordinate its activities with existing NANS structures, student unions and other stakeholders in the various zones. The association said its central objective was to translate the large student population into active participation in the electoral process, setting a target of 10 million students for the 2027 elections. “Our target is to facilitate the participation of at least 10 million Nigerian students in the 2027 General Elections,” the statement said. NANS also directed political support groups and election-related organisations seeking to engage students during the electoral period to liaise with the newly constituted committee. “On a final note, all political support groups and election-related organisations seeking to organise any political or election-related activities, sensitisation, mobilisation or engagements involving Nigerian students are expected to liaise with the NANS National Election Mobilisation Committee for proper coordination, notification and monitoring before organising any such activities,” the association said. The statement did not indicate that the committee would endorse or support any particular political party or candidate. Afeez charged members of the committee to approach their assignments with commitment and efficiency, expressing confidence in their ability to deliver on the mandate. “I have full confidence in each of you to deliver effectively in these responsibilities. I warmly congratulate you all, and as we move forward, I charge you to remain efficient, committed and dedicated to the responsibilities entrusted to you,” he said. The post NANS targets 10m students for 2027 elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Artisan Avenue : Une galerie de l'artisanat burkinabè ouvre ses portes à Ouagadougou
items.description: La Zone du Bois, à Ouagadougou, vient de s'enrichir d'un lieu où la matière prend vie sous les mains expertes des artisans. Artisan Avenue, galerie inaugurée ce samedi 3 octobre 2026, se veut plus qu'un espace de vente : un écrin où chaque objet raconte une histoire ; où le cuir, le coton, le bois et le métal se transforment en témoins silencieux d'un savoir-faire ancestral. Porté par Carine Traoré, le projet ambitionne d'offrir à l'artisanat burkinabè la reconnaissance qu'il mérite. Carine Traoré n'a pas conçu Artisan Avenue comme une simple vitrine commerciale, mais comme un acte de foi en la capacité de l'artisanat à traverser les époques sans se dénaturer. « Artisan Avenue est née d'une passion pour l'authenticité, la créativité et l'excellence de nos artisans », confie-t-elle, les yeux posés sur les pièces exposées. À Artisan Avenue, on vend aussi des sacs à main. Pour la promotrice, chaque objet qui prend place dans la galerie porte en lui la mémoire d'un geste répété, d'une technique transmise, d'une patience cultivée. « Notre motivation est simple, mais ambitieuse : donner davantage de visibilité aux producteurs, aux artisans, aux transformateurs et aux artistes qui, chaque jour, perpétuent les savoirs ancestraux tout en les réinventant pour répondre aux attentes du monde contemporain », précise-t-elle. Dans la galerie, on retrouve des montres en cuir qui épousent le poignet. Les chaussures et ceintures, taillées dans des cuirs locaux tannés selon des procédés traditionnels, portent en elles « la chaleur de la terre burkinabè. » Une cliente appréciant les chaussures exposées dans la galerie. Les sacs, véritables sculptures portatives, marient motifs et finitions d'une précision chirurgicale. Les pagnes, dont le célèbre Faso Danfani, déploient leurs fils de coton lourd tissés des mains des artisans burkinabè. « Chaque motif, chaque couleur, est le fruit d'un calcul ancestral, d'un langage codé que seuls les initiés savent déchiffrer. » Les tableaux et sculptures sur bois révèlent la patience des artisans, qui passent des jours à creuser, à polir, à faire émerger une forme de la matière brute. Les bracelets, réalisés à partir de perles de verre, de métaux récupérés ou de cauris, témoignent d'une créativité « qui s'adapte aux tendances sans renier ses racines ». Chaque perle enfilée est un acte de méditation, chaque assemblage une prière silencieuse. Des bracelets et plusieurs objets de la maroquinerie sont commercialisés dans la boutique. À Artisan Avenue, on retrouve aussi des épices pour la cuisine, du mobilier sculpté qui allie fonctionnalité et esthétique, des objets de design, etc. Quatre pôles, une philosophie Artisan Avenue s'articule autour de quatre axes. Le premier, dédié au commerce et à la création, vise à promouvoir les produits artisanaux et à soutenir les créateurs. Ici, les activités seront par exemple les participations à des forums nationaux et internationaux, des marchés de créateurs, des journées de découverte, des pop-up stores et des boutiques éphémères », détaille Carine Traoré. Des vêtements pour femme et homme sont aussi entreposés à Artisan Avenue. Le second pôle concerne la culture et les arts de vivre. After-work, dégustations de produits locaux, soirées thématiques ; la galerie se veut un lieu de convivialité où l'on vient autant pour acheter que pour ressentir. Le troisième axe porte sur l'impact social et l'engagement communautaire, à travers des programmes d'autonomisation économique et des partenariats avec des associations. Enfin, le dernier pôle est consacré à la transmission : ateliers créatifs pour enfants, initiation aux techniques artisanales, programmes de découverte du patrimoine culturel. Un lieu où l'art rencontre le quotidien « Nous rêvons de voir Artisan Avenue devenir une référence incontournable dans la promotion de l'artisanat d'excellence au Burkina Faso », se projette Carine Traoré. Pour elle, l'artisanat n'est pas qu'un secteur économique ; c'est un vecteur d'identité, un moyen de raconter le Burkina Faso au monde. Un espace pour se recréer. « Nous voulons que cette galerie soit un lieu vivant, un espace de rencontres, d'échanges, d'apprentissage et de découvertes », souligne la promotrice. Dans ce lieu, chaque objet n'est pas seulement à vendre, il est à contempler, à toucher, à comprendre car, selon la promotrice, derrière chaque pièce se cache un artisan, une histoire, un geste qui ne sera jamais tout à fait reproduit. Erwan Compaoré Lefaso.net

items.title: Fria : Tormelin s’adjudge le trophée Ahmed Kanté
items.description: Tormelin a remporté, samedi 3 octobre 2026, la finale du tournoi des vacanciers de Fria, en s’imposant face au Racing Club de Tigué à l’issue de la séance des tirs au but. La finale s’est disputée au stade Konko Sylla devant une forte mobilisation du public, après plus d’un mois de compétition. Les deux équipes se sont séparées sur un score nul et vierge au terme des 90 minutes. Tormelin a ensuite pris le dessus lors de la séance des tirs au but pour s’adjuger le trophée portant le nom d’Ahmed Kanté. Le tournoi était organisé par le District de football de Fria, avec l’appui de la Direction préfectorale de la Jeunesse et de la préfecture. La rencontre a enregistré la présence du préfet de Boffa, le colonel Mamadou Ciré Bah, du député de Fria, Coumbassa, et du préfet de Fria, le colonel Kalissa, ainsi que de plusieurs cadres d’AGB2A-GIC. L’entreprise minière, qui intervient notamment dans la zone de Tormelin, a accompagné la compétition dans le cadre de ses actions en faveur des communautés locales. AGB2A-GIC a notamment pris en charge le trophée principal, les médailles et les récompenses individuelles attribuées aux meilleurs acteurs de la compétition. L’entreprise a également fourni des maillots et des T-shirts à l’occasion des activités liées à la fête nationale du 2 octobre. Le partenariat se poursuit avec la préparation du prochain tournoi doté du trophée du Président. À l’occasion de la finale, AGB2A-GIC a remis le trophée, les médailles et plusieurs équipements destinés à accompagner cette nouvelle compétition. Les autorités de Boffa et de Fria ont salué cet appui aux initiatives sportives et communautaires. Le sacre de Tormelin clôt ainsi l’édition 2026 du tournoi des vacanciers de Fria. Au-delà de la compétition, l’événement a constitué un cadre de rassemblement pour les jeunes et les communautés locales, avec l’appui des autorités et de partenaires privés, dont AGB2A-GIC. Maïmouna Traoré

items.title: Crise agricole en Ukraine : Varsovie et Bucarest ferment la porte à de nouvelles aides à l'exportation des céréales
items.description: L'Ukraine pourrait etre confrontee a des difficultes dans le secteur agricole. Kiev demande a l'UE une aide accrue en matiere d'exportation de cereales, mais la Roumanie et la Pologne refusent de prendre des mesures supplementaires pour apporter leur soutien, a rapporte Politico en citant le ministre ukrainien de l'Agriculture, Tarass Vyssotsky. Selon le journal, ces deux pays detiennent une part essentielle des infrastructures de stockage et de transport des cereales. Cette semaine, le ministre ukrainien s'est rendu a Bruxelles pour demander une augmentation des volumes de produits transportes a travers l'Europe et l'octroi de 1,1 milliard d'euros afin de couvrir la hausse des coûts. Cependant, Bucarest et Varsovie ont repondu qu'elles ne pouvaient rien faire de plus. Le ministere roumain de l'Agriculture a notamment indique a Politico que les interets de ses propres agriculteurs restaient sa priorite. Selon le journal, les ports du pays sont deja surcharges en raison du faible niveau des eaux du Danube et de l'excedent de cereales en provenance d'Ukraine, ce qui empeche les agriculteurs locaux de vendre leur propre production. Le ministere polonais des Infrastructures a quant a lui souligne que Varsovie n'envisageait pas d'introduire des changements visant a accroître les volumes de transport de produits en provenance d'Ukraine. Les surfaces ensemencees en Ukraine pourraient diminuer de 40 % Les difficultes liees aux exportations pourraient entraîner des problemes au niveau des surfaces ensemencees en Ukraine. Selon Politico , si Kiev ne parvient pas a augmenter ses exportations vers l'Europe, ces surfaces devraient etre reduites de pres de 40 %. Ainsi, Tarass Vyssotsky a indique que les stocks de cereales et d'huile vegetale s'accumulent dans le pays, mais ne trouvent pas preneur. De ce fait, les agriculteurs se retrouvent prives des moyens necessaires pour semer les cultures d'hiver cette annee. Les difficultes rencontrees par l'agriculture ukrainienne surviennent dans un contexte d'enorme deficit budgetaire national, pour combler lequel Kiev a demande que soit acceleree l'octroi d'un pret de 90 milliards d'euros. L'UE refuse toutefois de ceder : selon Bloomberg, les responsables europeens estiment qu'un versement anticipe creerait des difficultes supplementaires de financement en 2027. Certains d'entre eux ont egalement exprime des doutes quant a certains chiffres presentes par Kiev concernant l'ampleur de ses besoins.

items.title: Northern senators seek reinforcement in Kopre-Sambisa corridor
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Senators from the 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory, under the aegis of the Northern Senators Forum (NSF), have called on the Federal Government and Defence Headquarters to urgently reinforce security presence in the Kopre-Sambisa corridor following reported insurgent attacks in Adamawa State. The senators also urged the authorities to adopt a unified and proactive strategy to tackle what they described as criminal enclaves in the area. The call followed attacks which the NSF said occurred between the night of September 30 and October 1, 2026, targeting communities and military outposts in Hong and Gombi Local Government Areas of Adamawa State. In a statement signed by the Chairman of the forum, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua, APC, Katsina Central, the senators expressed condolences to families who lost loved ones in the attacks. They specifically mentioned three soldiers of the 232 Battalion in Garaha, a forest guard and civilians among those reportedly killed. The senators also expressed concern over reports of abductions, destruction of property, burning of places of worship and the displacement of hundreds of residents from communities including Garaha, Dabna, Bangna, Mubang, Zah, Bitirhuya, Kwapre, Mayo Ladde, Gaya-Dlang, Garkida, Boima and Guyaku. The forum said the reported attacks on the 226 Battalion in Garkida and 232 Battalion in Garaha constituted a serious security concern for Adamawa State and the wider northern region. The statement said: “The Northern Senators Forum stands in solidarity with the people of Adamawa State. By our collective efforts, you will not be abandoned to terrorists.” The senators called on the Federal Government and Defence Headquarters to urgently reinforce security presence in the Kopre-Sambisa corridor and adopt a coordinated strategy to address the security situation. They also urged the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), North-East Development Commission (NEDC) and other humanitarian agencies to urgently provide relief materials, medical assistance and trauma support to people displaced by the attacks. The NSF further called on residents of Hong, Gombi and other parts of the country to remain vigilant and provide security agencies with actionable information. The senators expressed sympathy to the families of the deceased and prayed for the restoration of peace in Hong, Gombi, Adamawa State and the wider northern region. items.title: 4 injured Pakistanis rescued from vessel hijacked in Somalia arrive in Karachi with remains of 3 colleagues
items.description: The four Pakistanis who were injured during a security operation to recover a hijacked oil tanker off the coast of Somalia, along with the remains of three others who lost their lives in the episode, arrived in Karachi on Sunday evening. The crew members of MT Honour 25 reached Karachi after departing from Ethiopia’s capital Addis Ababa via Ethiopian Airlines flight ET 694. Sindh Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah, Labour Minister Saeed Ghani, PPP Senator Waqar Mehdi, MQM-P MNA Farooq Sattar and others welcomed the rescued seamen upon their arrival at Jinnah International Airport. Shah said the loss of lives and injuries was an “extremely regrettable incident” and extended his condolences to the bereaved families. The minister said all expenses for the treatment and care of the injured will be borne by the Sindh government, with the wounded to be taken to Aga Khan Hospital. Pakistan’s ambassadors to Djibouti and Ethiopia had seen off the four injured Pakistani crew members — Usman Ghani, Aqeel Khan, Ameen bin Shams and Yasir Khan — along with the mortal remains of Rafiullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmad Ansari from Addis Ababa. The seven were among 10 Pakistanis aboard MT Honour 25, which was hijacked by Somali pirates in April. Apart from Pakistanis, the vessel’s crew also included seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan. For around five months, there had been no progress either in negotiations or in the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages, despite concerns abounding about their declining health. Since the hijacking, the crew made several emotional videos and audio appeals , reporting that they ran out of clean water, food and medicine. For its part, FO maintained that it remained “actively engaged” to secure the release of the sailors. On Sept 29, Somali maritime police recovered the Palau-flagged oil tanker amid reports of casualties among the crew. During the operation, it said, 21 suspected pirates were apprehended, while operations to locate the remaining members continue. “Before the operation [had] begun, the pirates on board the ship killed five of the crew. Among those killed were three from Pakistan, one from Myanmar and one from India,” it said. Advocate Quratulain of the Ansar Burney Trust, however, gave a separate account of the events, saying the pirates had brought the hostages onto the deck when they realised Puntland forces were approaching. “They tied their hands and warned to kill them if the police force came anywhere near them without paying them the ransom,” she said, adding that the ransom demand had by then been reduced from an initial $3 million to $1m. She said the pirates opened fire on the hostages as the security forces proceeded with the operation, killing three Pakistanis, one Indian and one Myanmar national. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has announced a relief package worth Rs12.5 million for the deceased sailors’ families.

items.title: Navy disrupts 2 illegal refineries, recovers 58,000 litres
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has disrupted two illegal refining sites and recovered approximately 58,000 litres of products suspected to be stolen crude oil and illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in Rivers State. The operation was conducted by NNS Pathfinder, a unit under Operation Delta Sentinel, at Okarki Community in Ahoada West Local Government Area of the state on October 3, 2026. The Director of Information, Nigerian Navy, Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operation followed credible intelligence on suspected crude oil theft and illegal refining activities in the area. According to him, the naval team discovered nine dugout pits, storage containers and sacks containing the suspected stolen crude oil and illegally refined products at the sites. “The sites contained nine dugout pits, storage containers and sacks laden with the suspected stolen crude oil and illegally refined products,” he said. Folorunsho said the operation also disrupted the supply chain used by suspected criminal operators to store and process stolen petroleum resources. “The intervention further denied criminal operators access to facilities used to store and process stolen petroleum resources, disrupting the supply chain supporting illegal refining in the area,” he said. He added that the two illegal refining sites and recovered products were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures. No arrest was made during the operation, as the suspected operators reportedly fled before the arrival of the naval team. items.title: 2027: Enugu East is bleeding — Nweke
items.description: By Chinedu Adonu The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Enugu East Senatorial District, Chief Kingsley Nweke, has described the district as “bleeding”, urging journalists to remain courageous, professional and uncompromising in reporting issues affecting the people. Nweke spoke on Sunday after a novelty football match between the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Enugu State Council, and Nollywood actors at Ngwo Park, Achara Layout, Enugu. He said Enugu East needed a representative with the vision, capacity and preparedness to deliver effective services to the people. Nweke also urged journalists to uphold their responsibility of holding political leaders and public institutions accountable, stressing that the media should not compromise its role because of political or financial considerations. According to him, the challenges confronting the senatorial district require urgent attention, adding that journalists should continue to investigate and report issues affecting the welfare and development of residents. He urged media practitioners to adhere to the ethics of the profession and provide fair and balanced coverage to all political actors as the 2027 elections approach. He said: “Enugu East is bleeding. We cannot continue to pretend that all is well when our people are facing serious challenges. “The zone needs people with vision, capacity and integrity. I have been delivering good services to the people and wish to be there to accomplish what I have been doing. “This is why journalists must not compromise. The media remains one of the strongest institutions for defending democracy and giving voice to the voiceless.” The PDP candidate also urged political leaders and stakeholders in the district to place the interests of their constituents above personal and political considerations. He said the 2027 elections should provide an opportunity for voters to assess candidates based on their character, competence, records and capacity to effectively represent the people. items.title: Labour strike, referendum on Tinubu’s 2027 bid — Makinde campaign
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, MDPCO, has described the three-day warning strike by Nigerian workers as a referendum on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s bid for a second term, saying the action has exposed the consequences of his administration’s economic policies. For Nigerians struggling with rising living costs and shrinking purchasing power, the campaign said, the strike has sharpened the question of whether the Tinubu administration deserves another mandate in 2027. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Richard Ihediwa, MDPCO said the economic crisis that produced Labour’s Charter of Demands reflected the hardship caused by the administration’s policies. “The warning strike is a direct referendum on a failed government; a stark measure of how ill-conceived and ill-implemented economic policies have triggered widespread poverty in Nigeria,” it said. The campaign organization also questioned how the President could seek a second term after what it described as his government’s failure to shield Nigerians from the consequences of its policies. “We ask, how can a government that failed to shield its citizens from the consequences of its policies, credibly ask the same citizens to renew its mandate?” it asked. MDPCO faulted the administration over delayed and repeatedly rolled-over capital-budget implementation, continued borrowing, declining transparency and accountability, unfulfilled promises and what it described as elusive gains from subsidy removal. It further dismissed the government’s celebration of its economic reforms, arguing that the claimed gains remained largely disconnected from the daily reality of Nigerians. “Indeed, the continued celebration by the APC government of supposed gains of its economic reforms, when those claimed gains remain largely invisible in the daily lives of average Nigerians is self-delusional,” it said. The group called for people-centred reforms, transparent social safety nets and policies that would protect livelihoods while boosting national production. It said the proposed Makinde/Daura Presidency would pursue its RESET Nigeria Agenda, anchored on inclusiveness, national production, security, transparency and accountability. “The Makinde/Daura Presidency with its RESET Nigeria Agenda offers our nation a clear alternative with well thought-out, data-driven and people-friendly policies,” it said. MDPCO said Nigerians across party lines were rallying behind the APM presidential candidate, Engr. Seyi Makinde, ahead of the 2027 election, which it described as an opportunity to ‘RESET Nigeria’ into a nation that works for all. items.title: Police blur the line between invitations and arrests – Reindorf Twumasi Ankrah
items.description: Legal practitioner and Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Integrated Aluminium Development Corporation (GIADEC), Reindorf Twumasi Ankrah, has criticised law enforcement agencies for blurring the distinction between inviting citizens to assist investigations and placing them under arrest. Speaking to Samson Lardy on The Law on JoyNews on Sunday, October 4, 2026, he said the practice had created apprehension among people who might otherwise be willing to assist investigations. Mr Twumasi Ankrah explained that an invitation could be a request for information or documents to help investigators establish the facts, without the person being treated as a suspect. However, he said some people honoured such requests only to discover that they were no longer free to leave. “More often than not, you are invited, and being a law-abiding citizen who wants to see that justice is done or that truth is ascertained, you attend the invitation only to go there, and after giving the information that the police require from you, you are told you can’t leave,” he said. He argued that once a person’s freedom to leave was restricted, law enforcement officers must recognise the change in circumstances and take steps to safeguard the person’s constitutional rights. “At that particular point in time, the police is required by law to take certain steps to ensure that your constitutional rights are safeguarded. But mostly the police blur the line,” he stated. Mr Twumasi Ankrah acknowledged that inviting someone to assist an investigation was generally a prudent approach, particularly when investigators had yet to determine the person’s role in a case. He said the difficulty arose when invitations routinely resulted in arrests, leaving citizens uncertain about what to expect. “They have so often turned an invitation into an arrest that the people have now become apprehensive,” he said. According to him, the uncertainty had prompted some people to decline invitations and wait for law enforcement agencies to exercise their powers of arrest. He said citizens were consequently trying to balance their willingness to assist investigators with the need to protect their liberty. “There is this genuine fear… that when they go, there is a likelihood they won’t come back home. So, the police also have some work to do in that regard,” he added. The legal practitioner advised people attending police invitations to seek legal assistance, explaining that their status could change during questioning. “You go with your lawyer to pre-empt anything that may happen which was not within your contemplation,” he said. He stressed that legal representation could help individuals understand their position in an investigation and assert their rights if an invitation developed into an arrest.

items.title: Police rescue 42 kidnapped victims, arrest 96 suspects
items.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Police headquarters said on Sunday that Police operatives rescued 42 kidnapped victims, arrested 96 suspects victims in intelligence-led operations conducted across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory between September 26 and October 2, 2026. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Ineidu, who disclosed this in an operational report said the operations also led to the recovery of 16 firearms, 31 rounds of live ammunition and 16 vehicles, while two armed suspects were killed during the operations. Iniedu said the operations were conducted under the strategic leadership of the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, as the Force sustained its intelligence-led and community-based policing strategy. He said the 96 suspects were arrested in connection with various offences, including kidnapping, armed robbery, homicide, banditry, cultism, terrorism, cattle rustling and other criminal activities. He said the achievements went beyond statistics, noting that the operations had resulted in the rescue of victims, disruption of criminal networks and improved security in affected communities. According to the report, police operatives, tactical teams and personnel of the Nigerian Army in Sokoto State foiled a bandit attack and rescued 30 kidnapped victims. The bandits had reportedly blocked Katuru Village Junction and attacked vehicles conveying passengers returning from the weekly market at Tidibale Village before abducting them. The security operatives engaged the attackers in a gun duel, forcing them to flee into a nearby forest and abandon their victims. The 30 victims were rescued unhurt, while two persons who sustained gunshot wounds were taken to hospital for treatment. In Rivers State, police operatives attached to the Eliozu Division intercepted a suspected kidnap gang following a high-speed chase towards Rumuokoro. The operatives rescued a kidnapped victim and arrested one suspect, while an AK-47 rifle, three rounds of live ammunition and a tricycle were recovered. In Gombe State, a joint operation by the police, military, Department of State Services, hunters and vigilantes in Ribado Ward, through Bajoga in Funakaye Local Government Area, led to the arrest of four suspects and rescue of two kidnapped victims. The operation also resulted in the recovery of three motorcycles, while operational pressure reportedly forced fleeing gang members to release another victim the following day. In Kogi State, joint security forces rescued a telecoms worker who had been abducted by armed kidnappers dressed in military camouflage. The victim was part of a telecoms mast maintenance team abducted in the Kabba area. Four members of the team had escaped, while the rescued worker remained in captivity. The security forces sustained bush-combing and rescue operations, forcing the abductors to flee after teargas was deployed and enabling the victim to be rescued In Ondo State, operatives of the State Intelligence-led Violent Crime Response Unit, acting on credible intelligence, arrested two suspected members of an armed robbery syndicate in Akure. The suspects allegedly confessed to being members of a four-man syndicate operating in Akure and its environs. A subsequent raid on their hideout in the Olufoam area led to the recovery of a locally made four-round revolver, criminal charms, a laptop, motorcycle mirrors and a vehicle number plate. A third suspect was arrested the following day, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend the remaining member of the syndicate. In Delta State, police operatives rescued a 23-year-old woman who had been abducted and held for ransom. The victim was reportedly abducted on September 27, with the suspects demanding N245,000 for her release. Following a report lodged with the Anti-Vice Squad in Asaba, operatives tracked the suspects to their hideout, rescued the victim, and arrested six suspects comprising three males and three females. In Anambra State, 13 suspected cultists were arrested during a joint operation by the police and Agunechemba vigilante operatives in Okpoko. The operation, conducted in the early hours of September 28 following credible intelligence, also led to the recovery of suspected cannabis sativa, other illicit substances and six motorcycles. In Katsina State, police tactical teams foiled an attempted kidnapping along the Funtua-Zaria Highway at Dankawo Village. The suspects had reportedly blocked the highway to abduct commuters when operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, APC tactical teams and personnel of the 83 Police Mobile Force engaged them in a gun duel. The attackers fled into the bush, while subsequent combing operations led to the rescue of four kidnapped victims found inside a truck. Efforts were ongoing to establish the whereabouts of the driver and motor boy and arrest the fleeing suspects. In another operation in Katsina State, police recovered 159 electric detonators suspected to be components of improvised explosive devices during a stop-and-search operation along the Daura-Kongolam-Maiadua road The items were reportedly found in two bags inside a Toyota bus travelling from Kano towards Kongolam in Niger Republic. The 70-year-old driver was arrested after he allegedly failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for the items. The police said investigations were ongoing to establish the source, destination and intended use of the detonators and identify possible accomplices. In Benue State, police operatives arrested a suspected cultist who was allegedly threatening people with a firearm at a market square in Aliade. A search conducted on the suspect led to the recovery of an English pistol with five rounds of live ammunition, a locally fabricated pistol with four cartridges, and charms. Ineidu said all suspects arrested in the various operations remained in custody as investigations continued, while efforts were being made to apprehend other fleeing members of the criminal groups. He reaffirmed the commitment of the Nigeria Police Force to deepening intelligence-led policing, strengthening collaboration with communities and other security agencies, and sustaining operational pressure against criminal networks. The FPRO assured Nigerians that the Force would continue to protect lives and property, respond to threats to public safety, and bring criminal suspects to justice. items.title: Osun seeks to vacate order freezing accounts
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State Government has filed an application before the Federal High Court in Lagos seeking to set aside an ex-parte order freezing its accounts over a $13.9 million and N157.5 million arbitration award in favour of Gamji Nigeria Company Limited. Gamji, a contractor handling a water project in the state, had obtained the order directing the freezing of Osun State Government accounts with several commercial banks over the arbitration award. However, the state government, in a statement issued on Sunday by the Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Kolapo Alimi, alleged that the order was obtained through concealment of material facts. Alimi said the application to set aside the order was filed before the Federal High Court on October 2, 2026. He added that the arbitration award Gamji sought to enforce was also being challenged by the state government over what it described as irregularities in the arbitration process. According to him, the ex-parte order issued on September 9, 2026, referenced an alleged arbitral award said to have been made against the state in July 2024. “In fact, it was reported that the purported award which the ex-parte order of September 9, 2026 referenced does not exist, as there was no arbitral award made against the state government in July 2024. “The only arbitral award against the state government was in July 2026, and the said award is presently being challenged before the Lagos State High Court by the state government’s legal team,” he said. Giving the background to the dispute, Alimi said the contractual disagreement dated back to 2017, during the administration of former Governor Gboyega Oyetola, when the state rejected a variation request submitted by Gamji. He said the dispute centred on whether the state government was indebted to Gamji to the tune of $15,982,638.22. “The matter proceeded for arbitration which was deliberately mismanaged and handled to favour Gamji Nigeria Company Limited, while denying the state government fair hearing and full participation in the arbitration process as mandated by best practice in the arbitration process,” the statement alleged. Alimi said the state government had challenged what it described as irregularities in the arbitration proceedings and the final arbitral award before the Lagos State High Court. He further disclosed that counsel to the state government had filed the suit seeking to set aside the arbitral award at the Lagos State High Court on September 1, 2026. He said the suit was filed before Gamji subsequently approached the Federal High Court and obtained the ex-parte order freezing the state government’s accounts. The state government maintained that its legal team would continue to pursue the matter before the relevant courts.
