items.title: PTI terms access to Imran 'principal point of deadlock', claims Centre refused to include it in agreement
items.description: The PTI on Sunday asserted that the main reason for the breakdown of its talks with the Centre was that the latter refused to incorporate terms regarding access to incarcerated party founder Imran Khan into a proposed agreement. Hours-long negotiations yesterday between an opposition delegation comprising the PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP, ended in a deadlock. While the federal government blamed the PTI for the failure of negotiations, the main opposition party denied the allegations and claimed that the federal government was responsible for all that happened on Saturday night. In a press release posted on social media, the PTI expressed regret that the negotiations concluded without substantive progress, despite “serious efforts” to address concerns including political instability, access to the PTI founder as well as his medical treatment, and the worsening security situation in the country, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The statement said that the “principal point of the deadlock” was the party’s demand for immediate access to Imran, so that its leadership could consult him on matters of “national and political importance”. According to the statement, the government agreed to restore meetings between Imran and his family members and lawyers from Tuesday, but did not agree to the additional measures concerning his medical assessment and treatment. “In an effort to facilitate progress, the negotiating team conveyed that other demands could be set aside if the government agreed to this single request. However, according to PTI, the government declined to make access to Imran Khan part of the proposed agreement,” the PTI said. “PTI welcomed the resumption of family and legal meetings but stressed that such access cannot substitute for proper medical examination and necessary treatment,” the statement read, adding that the party called for Imran’s health to be addressed with “seriousness, transparency and humanitarian consideration”. The party stressed that just as leaders of other political parties remained central to decision-making and policy, the PTI must also be allowed to consult its chairman; restricting such consultation limited the scope for meaningful political engagement, it added. Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023, for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case . Despite an order by the Islamabad High Court (IHC) allowing him twice-a-week meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays with his family, lawyers and other associates, Imran has been restricted from meeting visitors for several months. His health has deteriorated over the course of his prison sentence, prompting outcry from members of the party. According to the PTI, Imran’s health and medical treatment were also raised as a matter of fundamental importance in the talks, with the negotiating team seeking immediate access to him, his transfer to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for treatment, and the constitution of an “appropriate” medical board — including his personal physician — to ensure his proper examination, diagnosis and treatment. After his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January, Imran has been provided with treatment at the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims). In mid-August, the Supreme Court ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment. However, the government later revealed that Imran was instead taken to Pims , prompting a strong reaction from his family and party. Security situation in KP The security situation in KP also featured prominently in the discussions, with the PTI saying it stressed that the concerns of the public must remain central to counterterrorism policies. According to the statement, the Centre sought the provincial government’s “unconditional support” for its counterterrorism measures and operations as well as support for imposing emergency measures within 72 hours in the merged districts and adjoining areas. “The PTI reiterated its unequivocal condemnation of terrorism and stressed that eliminating terrorism, protecting citizens and restoring lasting peace must remain a national priority,” it said, adding that the party paid tribute to the officers and personnel of the authorities that have sacrificed their lives in the fight against terrorism and expressed solidarity with civilians and families who had suffered from terrorist violence. “Terrorism cannot be defeated through force alone or through unilateral measures that could expose innocent civilians to further loss of life, property or displacement,” the party maintained, calling for a strategy that combined “firm action against terrorism with protection of civilian populations and sensitivity to local realities”. Accordingly, it proposed a meeting within 72 hours of authorised representatives of the federal and provincial governments to develop a mutually agreed strategy for peace and counterterrorism. It also proposed consultation with political parties represented in the KP Assembly, elected representatives, tribal elders and other relevant stakeholders in order for the policy to enjoy public confidence and be implemented effectively. PTI also rejected attempts to characterise the position of KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as political obstinacy, arguing that “had access to Imran Khan been facilitated, the chief minister could have consulted the PTI chairman directly on security and counterterrorism policy, potentially helping to bridge differences and create greater consensus”. Responding to the press conference held by federal ministers after the talks ended without result, PTI said the government should address the substantive issues that prevented progress instead of seeking to place the responsibility on the opposition. It called for an explanation as to why immediate access to Imran was considered unacceptable, why requests regarding his medical care were not accommodated, and why the proposed broader consultative approach was not accepted for developing a sustainable security strategy in KP. The party reiterated that it remains “prepared to engage in political dialogue, constitutional processes, meaningful consultation and national consensus to address Imran Khan’s health and treatment, restoration of democracy, supremacy of the Constitution and law, political stability, terrorism and the wider challenges confronting Pakistan”. The party stressed, however, that “meaningful negotiations” could not succeed through predetermined positions or demands for unconditional endorsement. “Serious dialogue requires flexibility, mutual confidence, consultation and a genuine willingness to translate discussions into practical progress,” the statement added. ‘Three fundamental red lines’ Separately, Opposition Chief Whip Malik Aamir Dogar stated that the talks had fallen through on “three fundamental red lines”: meetings with Imran, his medical treatment, and KP’s terrorism policy. “We made it clear that the authority to call off the long march rests solely with Imran Khan sahib , so a meeting with him is essential,” he said in a post on X. The MNA added that, when the government was unwilling to do this, an alternative demand for Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas’s meeting with Imran was also put forward, but similarly rejected. On the PTI founder’s health, Dogar said that the opposition’s minimum demand had been the inclusion of his personal physicians in his treatment to dispel “doubts and suspicions” about his health. This, too, was not agreed to, which heightened the opposition’s concerns. The third “red line”, he said, was that the opposition demanded that “no decision be made unilaterally” regarding KP’s security and terrorism policy, but rather that all relevant stakeholders be taken into confidence. “Instead of broad consultations on this matter, the government sought hasty decisions within 72 hours,” he said. As a result of the government’s refusal of these demands and the party’s refusal to back down from them, he added, the negotiations ended in a deadlock. Salman Akram notes Centre’s ‘insistence on unilateral’ CT measures Earlier, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja asserted that the main reason for the breakdown of talks with the Centre was the latter’s insistence on “unilateral” counter-terrorism measures in KP. In a post on X, Raja wrote that the “primary reason for the failure of the talks around 3am this morning” was that the “PTI-TTAP team stood firm on its principled position that anti-terrorism actions in KPK would be based on agreement between the federal government and the KPK government”. He said the opposition wanted those actions to be “framed on the basis of consultation with, and the buy-in of, the different political parties represented” in the KP Assembly. “This was not acceptable to the government team, that insisted that all actions unilaterally initiated by it would have to be owned by the provincial government,” Raja asserted. “The PTI-TTAP team was clear that we have zero tolerance for terrorism and are committed to rooting it out. We also have a clear position against so-called collateral damage in the form of innocent lives and internal displacement of the local population.” Raja noted that counterterrorism policies require support from the local population and ground intelligence. “The wisdom provided by the jirga held in the KP assembly of all the political and tribal notables of the province, including the merged districts, must be heeded. “This was not acceptable to the federal government,” he wrote. In November last year, a peace jirga held at the KP Assembly, also attended by the governor, demanded that the Centre consult the KP government over Afghan policy. Tarar accuses KP govt of ‘supporting’ terrorism On the other hand, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar responded to Raja in a lengthy post on X, questioning why the KP government has not taken action against terrorism. “It is only now, when your KP government is politically weak, [that] you have started responding to the federal government’s calls for [a] joint mechanism to fight terrorism, that too only as a strategy to save your political capital in KP,” the minister alleged. “This is an old strategy of PTI, that when under pressure, they start talking of consultations and joint actions, but on [the] ground they do the exact opposite.” Accusing the KP government of “double standards and hypocrisy”, Tarar contended that while it said it was taking steps to fight terrorism, its “narrative on terrorism is in favour of terrorists”. “KPK government’s policy only encourages and supports [the] spread of terrorism in the province,” the PML-N leader alleged. Tarar questioned why the KP government had not taken steps against terrorism or convened the provincial apex committee for meetings and why it had not condemned the “TTA regime for sponsoring terrorism inside Pakistan and conduct of cross-border attacks on the posts and drone attacks by them”. “Why hasn’t the KPK Government not implemented NAP as per which clear action is required against illegal spectrum, illegal Afghan immigrants, measures for capacity enhancement of Police and [Counter-Terrorism Department]?” he added. He asked why PTI leaders did not visit checkposts of security forces and police to express their support, and whether they had taken interest in the governance and development of esrtwhile Fata. The minister urged the PTI to “stop selling this false narrative of collective consultations, jirgas or any other method, as this means nothing on [the] ground other than delaying tactics”. Tarar reiterated his comments in a televised video statement, slamming the PTI for failing to abandon “double standards and hypocrisy”, which he said resulted in deadly terrorist attacks in KP. “We were considering that they may go back on their word, and I had been saying it for the past two and a half weeks: if we are going to talk, then who should we talk to? And if we talk, what guarantee do we have that they will honour their word?” the minister asked. He accused the PTI of taking U-turns and “expressing pride in them”, as well as failing to maintain a steady stance on the issue of protecting the lives and property of KP’s residents. “Now different statements are emerging: Salman Akram Raja is saying one thing; [Adviser to KP Chief Minister on Information] Shafi Jan is saying that they want to change the policy on terrorism,” he added. “What is your policy? Does it even exist?” Tarar alleged: “The only policy you have is deliberately supporting terrorism. Your policy is how you can elevate terrorists, how you can build a political terror-crime nexus and how you can spread terrorism across the province. “I said earlier that you have to decide whether you stand with Pakistan or Afghanistan. You take the benefits of Pakistan, but are in favour of Afghanistan.” “The policy change they are talking about is to give terrorists cover and protection,” Tarar further claimed. He said people of KP were being killed in terrorist incidents because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi “wants to free one prisoner”. “Lives have been wasted and people have been martyred because the province’s CM prioritises the release of one convicted prisoner,” he insisted. “This is why I say they (PTI) are TTP’s (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) B-team and TTA’s (Afghan Taliban) C-team,” the PML-N leader alleged. The minister further accused the KP government of having a “pro-terrorism mindset”, which he contended had contributed to a failure to prevent terrorist attacks and cross-border firing from Afghanistan. “Because their mindset is pro-terrorism, then they don’t care that security forces, armed forces, police, and thousands of officers and troops have been martyred,” Tarar claimed. “They cannot even honour their martyrs … They burned the Chagai monument in Peshawar. This is a terrorist mindset; can they stop terrorism with this mindset in govt? No, they never will,” the minister asserted. The minister continued denouncing the PTI, accusing it of not building a forensic lab or creating a Counter-Terrorism Department, failing to install Safe City cameras and being unable to fortify police check posts. “You’ll be surprised to know that since they took power, they have received over Rs700 billion for counter-terrorism under the NFC Award,” Tarar claimed, adding that it is “extra”. “This year, if you look at the figures, they have earmarked Rs45bn for police capacity building and counter-terrorism, but only released Rs1.5bn. The rest is for salaries and expenses. Is this how the war on terrorism will be fought?” he asked. Earlier on Sunday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that the weekend talks collapsed as the PTI had initiated its long march , accusing KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of “sabotaging” the negotiations. “Their team was reasonable. I am repeating that I will not blame anyone else for all of this collapsing. There is only one person responsible for the entire collapse, and that is the KP chief minister,” the interior minister declared. He further said that Afridi was to be responsible “if there is any loss of life”. He said those supporting the PTI leader should “realise that they will be committing contempt of court, and we will take legal action against them to every possible extent”.

items.title: An SNL Sketch That Understands How the Internet Shapes Our Reality
items.description: Sharing the culture you love—a beloved song, that book that changed your life—can help translate your inner world to the people you love. Or it might make you look really strange. So it goes in one sketch from last night’s Saturday Night Live , in which a trio of teen girls at a sleepover (played by Sarah Sherman, Veronika Slowikowska, and Jane Wickline) take turns playing clips of their favorite get-ready-with-me videos, the popular format where content creators dress and prepare themselves for the day ahead. Two of the girls share par-for-the-course videos, before Sherman’s character introduces everyone to the influencer she loves the most: @ColoradoVicky1 (Dakota Johnson, the show’s host), a woman whose life doesn’t seem so aspirational. As she smiles cheerfully, her eyes vacant, Vicky invites her audience to “get ready with me for court-ordered electroshock therapy.” In another clip, she styles herself in green lipstick and a Teletubby-esque antenna in preparation for getting “5150’d on the roof of a San Bernardino Whole Foods.” “She seems … unwell,” says Slowikowska’s character. But Sherman’s teen girl pays no mind to such judgments, or to her friend’s question about how she even found this account, whose videos don’t even have double-digit views. “I’m legiterally addicted to her ass,” Sherman says. “Guess my algorithm is just cool-mazing?!” These days, everyone uses a different internet. Algorithms serve up specialized content catered to each user’s unique interests, creating a warped mirror of their own reality, and last night’s sketch cleverly captured the disconnect that sometimes arises when people reveal their private online consumption to one another. @ColoradoVicky1’s behavior only gets more bizarre the more clips the girls watch. Without blinking once, Vicky explains that her “outfit of the day” is a pair of handcuffs, which she plans to use to attach herself to the actor who plays Turtle in Entourage . She one-ups this proclamation with an even stranger how-to video, in which she asks viewers to tag along as she makes brunch and gives herself a lobotomy. (“You’re gonna want to start by finding a really good power drill,” she monotones.) [ Read: The loneliness crisis hits SNL ] Sherman’s friends seem to get progressively more put off by her media diet. It doesn’t help that Sherman’s character isn’t the only one in the house who could probably stand to log off. Every few minutes, her dad (James Austin Johnson) comes into the room with snacks and immediately reveals how depressed he is: “I’m just gonna go drink in the pool for a while, stand in the deep end,” he announces, before leaving the room. When the sleepover guests are concerned, Sherman explains that her dad is just in a funk: His boss discovered he dresses up like Sailor Moon, and he just found out that Draft Kings uses real money. His particular online milieu is bleeding into, and beginning to harm, his real-life existence. When her friends ask if they should get help, Sherman’s character insists that they “stop giving him attention—that’s, like, exactly what he wants.” She continues to ignore his not-so-subtle cries for help, until the sketch’s ending beat, in which he randomly shows up in @ColoradoVicky1’s livestream as her new lover. Sherman seems thrilled by this development, announcing that Vicky is going to be her new mom. Finally, her father’s real-life depression is good for something. Teen girls and their dads alike are vulnerable to having their minds and lives warped by their feeds, the sketch warns. And once brought to light, these online rabbit-holes might not translate so well to real life: The sketch-comedy version of this is funny because it’s so familiar, while the fracturing of reality outside SNL is mostly just unnerving.

Dans cette quatrieme etape d'une tournee programmee de plus de 3 600 km sur 30 etapes au total dans le pays, elle a ete accueillie par une ferveur populaire peu commune. La ville a exalte les valeurs de l'olympisme de paix, de solidarite et de fraternite qui font egalement partie de l'identite meme de la ville, fondee il y a quelque 300 ans. Ces valeurs ont ete justement soulignees par l'adjoint au maire Alioune Badara Diop, present lors de la ceremonie d'accueil de la flamme dans sa ville. « L'olympisme, c'est la paix, la solidarite et la fraternite, des valeurs auxquelles on reconnaît la ville de Saint-Louis, qui a joue un role important dans le sport senegalais », a-t-il declare a l'agence de presse senegalaise (APS). La flamme olympique sur le fleuve Sénégal à Saint-Louis 🛶🇸🇳🤩 #Dakar2026 #PassTheEnergy https://t.co/9Ip1Dl4jDh — Dakar 2026™ (@jojdakar2026) October 3, 2026 S'exprimant au nom du gouverneur de la region, face a une foule en liesse, l'adjoint du prefet de Saint-Louis, Abdou Khadre Dieylani Ba, a lance : « Saint-Louis est une ville historique, culturelle et sportive. J'invite la jeunesse et les populations de Saint-Louis a s'approprier cet evenement pour la reussite totale de son organisation. » 🇸🇳 Au #Sénégal, la flamme olympique poursuit sa tournée à un mois des JOJ Dakar 2026 Elle fait étape ce samedi à Saint-Louis, première capitale de l’#Afrique-Occidentale française, alors que la ville mène une vaste campagne de rebaptisation des rues. https://t.co/qDDlJWsxio — RT en français (@RTenfrancais) October 3, 2026 Une traversee memorable de Saint-Louis La flamme olympique a ete portee par deux athletes natifs de la region, qui ont brille dans leurs disciplines respectives, selon le correspondant de RT dans la ville de Saint-Louis. Il s'agit d'Ousseynou Diop, nageur, et de Fary Seye, ancienne judokate et desormais arbitre internationale, qui l'ont transportee a bord des pirogues pour traverser le fleuve Senegal et passer sous le majestueux pont Faidherbe, dans un moment a la symbolique forte alliant l'histoire de la region, sa culture et son avenir porte par sa jeunesse. 🇸🇳 L'équipe de RT en français est au nord du Sénégal De Saint-Louis à Matam, vous aurez toutes les informations liées au séjour de la flamme olympique dans cette partie du pays dans les prochains jours. https://t.co/yQaeF5zkBh — RT en français (@RTenfrancais) October 2, 2026 Les autorites de la ville ont prepare des festivites et des animations sportives et culturelles pour l'occasion, avec la mise en valeur des sites emblematiques de la region, ainsi que son patrimoine culturel de musique et de danse, entre autres prestations artistiques, artisanales et creatives. items.title: UK's Green Party adopts 'Zionism is racism' policy
items.description: The UK’s left-wing Green Party on Sunday voted to define Zionism as racism at the party’s annual get-together, drawing sharp backlash from British Jewish groups and the Israeli government. Members of the Greens, which has five members in Britain’s 650-seat parliament and which enjoyed a boost in recent local and special elections, backed the motion at the party’s conference, with 1,022 votes in favour and 813 against. According to the motion, Zionism would be “treated as any other form of racism”, and the party supports the establishment of a “single democratic Palestinian State in all of historic Palestine”. “This has been a serious and deeply felt debate within our membership,” a Green spokesperson said. Later, the party issued a joint statement by Leader Zack Polanski, its co-deputy leaders and five MPs noting that it will not tolerate discrimination. “We will continue to stand in opposition to genocide, ethnic cleansing, apartheid and the illegal occupation,” the statement reads. “We will continue to call out the heinous crimes of the Netanyahu government, and we will continue to work to ensure that the Green Party is an anti-racist party in every way. It adds, “We know there is no conflict between supporting the rights of Palestinians and the rights of Jewish people.” The Greens have enjoyed a surge in popularity under Polanski’s charismatic leadership, attracting voters dissatisfied with the centre-left Labour government’s stance on Israel’s military campaign in Gaza. However, Polanski’s popularity has taken a hit in recent months, polls show, following several missteps. “This motion would make the Green Party the first electorally significant UK political party in living memory to adopt what appears to be an overtly antisemitic political platform,” three Jewish community groups said in a letter to the party ahead of the vote. “We also emphasised the implications for the safety and welfare of all British Jews,” the heads of the Board of Deputies, Community Security Trust and Jewish Leadership Council warned. Israel’s foreign ministry said the policy went “far beyond the boundaries of legitimate political debate”. “Every political party in Britain, first and foremost the governing Labour Party, must unequivocally reject this twisted resolution,” it said. The motion laid bare divisions in the party, with Polanski — who is currently running to become an MP in former prime minister Keir Starmer’s London constituency — skipping the vote. Despite at least three out of five Green MPs opposing the motion, Polanski said earlier this week that the “displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people” was “clearly racism”. United Nations investigators have accused Israel of committing “genocide” in the war in Gaza, a finding that Israel has rejected.

items.title: Sebta : plus de 3 000 migrants concernés par le démantèlement du camp d’El Tarajal
items.description: La Police nationale espagnole, appuyée par des unités de l’armée, a lancé ce dimanche matin une opération d’évacuation et de démantèlement d’une partie du camp de migrants installé sur la plage de « El Tarajal » dans la ville occupée de Sebta. Cette opération de grande ampleur vise l’un des principaux campements informels apparus dans la ville au cours des dernières semaines. Selon l’agence EFE, le camp compte plus de 3 000 migrants, tandis que la police locale estime que leur nombre pourrait dépasser 3 500 personnes. L’opération a débuté aux premières heures de dimanche, avec la participation d’unités d’intervention de la Police nationale espagnole et de plus de 30 véhicules de police, ainsi que de véhicules blindés de type BMR et d’un véhicule VAMTAC, dans le cadre d’un important dispositif de sécurité. La première phase de l’opération s’est concentrée sur la partie située à proximité de la station de dessalement, les autorités cherchant à évacuer la zone et à sécuriser les abords de l’installation. L’opération a été organisée en plusieurs étapes en raison du nombre élevé de personnes présentes dans le camp et de l’insuffisance des capacités d’hébergement pour accueillir tout le monde en une seule fois. Les personnes concernées par l’évacuation seront transportées en bus vers le Centre temporaire d’accueil des étrangers (CATE), situé dans le secteur de Tarajal, où elles feront l’objet de procédures de tri et d’identification avant que leur destination ultérieure ne soit déterminée. Selon les médias espagnols, les autorités offrent aux migrants marocains transférés à Tarajal la possibilité d’un retour volontaire au Maroc. Plus de 150 Marocains auraient choisi, selon des données locales publiées dimanche, de regagner le Maroc par le poste-frontière après leur arrivée depuis le camp. Une situation similaire s’était produite lors du démantèlement du camp de la plage de Benítez plus tôt dans la semaine, une opération qui avait été marquée par des troubles. L’opération menée à « El Tarajal » intervient dans le contexte de la crise migratoire qui a suivi l’entrée collective de migrants à Sebta fin juillet, entraînant l’installation de campements temporaires dans plusieurs secteurs de la ville. Les autorités affirment que les conditions de vie dans le camp sont devenues plus dangereuses avec l’arrivée de l’automne, notamment en raison des pluies, des vents marins et du risque de tempêtes. Des médias espagnols ont également fait état de préoccupations liées à l’hygiène et à la qualité de l’eau. Le gouvernement espagnol cherche à achever le démantèlement du camp d’« El Tarajal » au plus tard le 15 octobre. L’opération intervient quelques jours avant la visite prévue du roi Felipe VI et de la reine Letizia à Sebta, le 13 octobre. Le manque de capacités d’accueil constitue l’un des principaux obstacles à une évacuation complète, après que la saturation des structures d’hébergement a déjà conduit certains migrants à retourner dans les zones côtières. Avec le début du démantèlement d’« El Tarajal », la crise des campements de migrants à Sebta entre dans une nouvelle phase, alors que le nombre de Marocains ayant choisi de retourner volontairement au Maroc augmente. Selon des déclarations rapportées par des médias locaux du ministre espagnol de la Politique territoriale et chargé de la coordination unifiée, Ángel Víctor Torres, plus de 9 000 Marocains seraient retournés volontairement au Maroc depuis le 10 août. Le démantèlement des campements encore présents devrait se poursuivre dans les prochains jours. items.title: Mamou : un accident de moto fait deux morts et un blessé grave à Sokotoro
items.description: Un accident de la circulation impliquant une moto et un camion stationné sur la chaussée a fait deux morts et un blessé grave, samedi 3 octobre, aux environs de 19 heures, à Sokotoro, dans la préfecture de Mamou. Selon les informations, la moto transportait trois personnes qui revenaient du marché hebdomadaire de Saramoussaya en direction de Sokotoro. En cours de route, l’engin à deux roues a violemment percuté un camion immobilisé sur la chaussée. La violence du choc a coûté la vie au conducteur de la moto et à l’une des deux passagères. La seconde passagère, grièvement blessée, a été évacuée au centre de santé de Timbo avant d’être transférée à l’hôpital régional de Mamou pour une prise en charge médicale. D’après les informations, l’accident s’est produit dans un virage. L’absence de signalisation permettant d’alerter les usagers de la route sur la présence du camion stationné aurait rendu la situation particulièrement dangereuse. Ce nouveau drame relance la question du stationnement des véhicules sur la chaussée, particulièrement dans les virages et les zones à faible visibilité.

items.title: Turning invitations into arrests is making citizens reluctant to assist police – Twumasi Ankrah
items.description: Private legal practitioner Reindorf Twumasi Ankrah has warned that the practice of arresting people after inviting them to assist investigations is making citizens increasingly reluctant to cooperate with the police. Mr Twumasi Ankrah, who is the acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Integrated Aluminium Development Corporation (GIADEC), said the uncertainty surrounding such invitations had created fear among people willing to provide information to investigators. Speaking to Samson Lardy on The Law on JoyNews on Sunday, October 4, 2026, he argued that law enforcement agencies must address the apprehension their practices had generated. “The practice has shown over the years that when people willingly submit themselves or attend to an invitation extended to them by the police or any other institution with the power to effect arrest, they end up being arrested,” he said. According to him, some citizens now prefer to wait for a formal arrest rather than voluntarily honour an invitation that could result in unexpected detention. “So, with the benefit of that practice, people now have also taken a position not to honour such invitations and to say to them that you come and now exercise your powers of arrest; then they know that properly they are a suspect,” he explained. Mr Twumasi Ankrah acknowledged that invitations were a legitimate and prudent means of obtaining information, particularly when investigators had not established whether an individual should be considered a suspect. An invitation, he explained, could simply require someone to supply documents or clarify facts relevant to a case involving another person. However, he said the repeated use of invitations that subsequently led to arrests had undermined citizens’ confidence in the process. “They have so often created, turned an invitation into an arrest that the people have now become apprehensive,” he stated. He said this had left citizens balancing their willingness to help investigators establish the truth against concerns about their personal liberty. “There is this genuine fear as to whether it is imminent or remote, that when they go, there is a likelihood they won’t come back home. So, the police also have some work to do in that regard,” he said. Mr Twumasi Ankrah advised individuals to seek legal representation when attending an invitation, given the possibility that their role in an investigation could change. “You go with your lawyer to pre-empt anything that may happen which was not within your contemplation,” he said. He further argued that once officers prevented an individual from leaving, they had to recognise the change from voluntary attendance to detention and safeguard the person’s constitutional rights.

items.title: Naqvi says talks with opposition have collapsed, accuses KP CM of 'sabotaging' negotiations
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Sunday that the talks between the federal government and the opposition had collapsed as the PTI had initiated its long march, accusing Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of “sabotaging” the negotiations. Naqvi was addressing a press conference in Islamabad hours after an hours-long second round of talks between the two sides ended without yielding any results. “Their team was reasonable. I am repeating that I will not blame anyone else for all of this collapsing. There is only one person responsible for the entire collapse, and that is the KP chief minister,” the interior minister declared. He further said that Afridi was to be responsible “if there is any loss of life”. He said those supporting the PTI leader should “realise that they will be committing contempt of court, and we will take legal action against them to every possible extent”. He warned that no one would be allowed to violate the Islamabad High Court’s order regarding protest. The IHC order , issued on Sept 14, ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”. Notably, Naqvi stressed that there “had been no request from our side for the long march to be postponed”. “When we had the first meeting, we told them that the long march was not an issue for us. However, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto had already given an indication and had also given a date. A day earlier, he had said that the PPP wanted the long march to be postponed and for the temperature to be brought down,” he added. Naqvi explained that the PTI was given the option to hold a protest but would not allow an attempt to “create a disturbance”. “We gave them this option. Now, if they violate the orders, whether they are workers or politicians, whether they are protesting within KP or outside KP, we will pursue them one by one. This time, we want to ensure that this repeated episode of creating a disturbance in Islamabad comes to an end,” he asserted. According to the interior minister, there were two agreements to be reached — one was a “main agreement” that would cover whatever was being decided with the opposition parties, and the other was regarding counterterrorism. “If we had known that no one in this committee was authorised to give a commitment on behalf of the KP government, or that the KP government would veto all these things, we would not have held the negotiations in this form in the first place,” he remarked. The minister said the two sides had agreed “100 per cent on political things” so that the KP government could come on board with the Centre on the counterterrorism issues. “It is not appropriate that there is a war going on in one province and the ministers there are giving statements against the army, are not coming to funerals, and at the local level, somewhere or the other, terrorists are also being given support,” he added. “If there is a military operation, would you tell the army which gun to use or which drone to use? This happens nowhere in the world,” he said. Naqvi detailed Saturday’s developments: “I requested CM Afridi to onboard the KP government because, definitely, the problems we are facing are coming from the KP government. He said, ‘Okay, I am going now,’ so we postponed the meeting until tomorrow. All members agreed to the postponement. “They (opposition team) held negotiations with CM Afridi for four hours. The KP CM gave them his feedback and gave them the mandate that whatever they finalise with him, they should proceed with it.” The interior minister accused Afridi of changing the draft of the agreement despite what had been agreed to earlier. “When I forwarded the draft to the KP chief minister, around 9pm he became active. Once the draft is finalised, he asks for changes once and then asks again, and by 12am or 12:30am at night, he brings an entirely new draft. And in that, he changed the things that we had locked after discussing them,” Naqvi asserted. In an apparent jibe at the KP CM, Naqvi noted that placing “immature and inexperienced people in positions of authority had consequences for the country”. “You have seen in the past how chief ministers came to this province and the country continued to suffer the consequences. Similarly, if an immature boy sits in a position of authority, has no experience and has not seen politics, then definitely he will call himself a representative of the people, but he will make decisions in the same way as my team and I witnessed yesterday.” Commending the government’s delegation, the minister said: “They worked non-stop for 12 hours and, even before that, made sincere efforts to resolve the issue. I will give them credit for the fact that at no point did they say no. They remained focused on resolving the matter. From the smallest issue to the major ones, all the members made a sincere effort to resolve them in a good manner.” Naqvi meets Kundi at Governor House Naqvi then went to Peshawar, where he met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. According to a statement issued by the Governor House, both leaders expressed concerns over the “risk of facilitating terrorists to safely cross security checkposts” during the PTI’s Islamabad march. They agreed that whenever the president and the prime minister deemed it necessary to impose governor’s rule or emergency to “save the province from terrorism and destruction, the Governor’s House will play a full Constitutional role”. The interior minister and the governor discussed important matters at the provincial level, including growing unrest in the province, the political scenario, and the situation arising from the Islamabad march. The statement read that the KP government’s attitude during the negotiation regarding counterterrorism actions was tantamount to enmity toward the people and the province. Naqvi and Kundi also termed the use of helicopters and other government resources by Afridi and the provincial ministers for the march as a “blatant violation” of the IHC verdict. Other matters of mutual interest were also discussed in the meeting, and consultations were held on numerous issues, according to the statement. Kundi said in his own statement that KP Inspector General of Police Zulfikar Hameed was also present at the meeting, which revolved around the prevailing security situation in the province. “The security of our people remains our foremost priority. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has sacrificed enough, and every institution must work together to protect our people and defeat terrorism,” the governor said. Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif visited Naqvi’s residence to offer condolences over the death of his maternal uncle, Akmal Hussain Naqvi. According to the PM Office, the interior minister also briefed PM Shehbaz in detail on the “key negotiations held last night and the progress made” so far. Conditions and demands Earlier in the day, Naqvi also claimed on X that the KP government had agreed to sign a written agreement and submit an implementation plan within 72 hours, mainly covering counterterrorism initiatives, during the talks held over the weekend, but then backtracked. According to Naqvi, the PTI had agreed to: Reconsider the Police Act 2026 in light of the security situation and the need to protect security matters from political interference Prevent terrorists from operating freely or finding safe havens in the province Unequivocal condemnation of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and all other terrorist groups Support the national policy on Afghan refugees, including repatriation and dismantling Afghan camps in KP No contact with the interim Afghan government Substantial funding for counterterrorism operations and the police Full provincial ownership of counterterrorism measures and stronger cooperation with the armed forces Decisions on counterterrorism in the former Fata and merged districts Implementation of the National Action Plan “Last night, during the final phase of negotiations, the KP government backed out of these commitments. Security must not be politicised while the province is at war,” he said. The meeting between the opposition and federal government at Parliament House began after 4pm on Saturday, with discussions focusing on the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad. The talks extended into the early hours of Sunday without yielding any results. However, shortly before 3am on Sunday, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, who was part of the opposition delegation, told the media that the talks had not resulted in a breakthrough. He went on to say that the deadlock was over jailed PTI founder Imran Khan’s meeting with his personal physicians, and how to address terrorism in KP. But Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, who was part of the government’s delegation, said the talks failed primarily because the “KP government could not assure whether they would cooperate in the fight against terrorism in the future”. He alleged that the PTI’s provincial government in KP did not want to implement the NAP and that the PTI delegation that participated in the talks had also left the venue “disappointed because the KP government did not cooperate on terrorism”. Following these allegations, CM Afridi posted on X that he was sharing the text of the draft he sent to the opposition’s negotiating team, saying that “no even one demand in there was unconstitutional or illegal”. He then went on to list the demands, calling for: Arrangements for meetings between the prime minister and the leaders of the opposition in both houses of Parliament to discuss important political, national, constitutional, legal, and democratic issues, particularly those facing delays. “The two sides shall be bound to ensure effective and feasible progress within two months towards resolving the aforementioned matters through mutual consultation and negotiations.” The prime minister to form a joint political negotiating committee comprising representatives from the ruling coalition, the PPP and opposition parties. “This committee shall engage in continuous negotiations with the opposition on national and political matters, points of disagreement, and other important issues, and shall seek feasible solutions through mutual consensus. The committee shall ensure significant progress on negotiations and resolutions within one month of its formation and shall present its recommendations to the relevant leadership.” Ensuring all legal, human and medical rights for Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, in accordance with the jail manual, Constitution and prevailing laws. “Where legally applicable, necessary medical facilities and treatment shall be provided to them, taking into account the opinion, instructions and advice of their personal or nominated physicians.” Allowing Imran and Bushra Bibi to meet their family members, lawyers and other associates, in accordance with the jail manual and relevant laws. “Such meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the law and jail rules and regulations. However, the facility of meetings will not be used by any party for political or other purposes prohibited by law.” The process of taking up appeals filed by prisoners against their sentences to be initiated or completed within 10 days, where legally possible, in accordance with the Constitution and law. “All cases shall be decided by the relevant courts and legal forums in accordance with the Constitution, law, transparent judicial procedures and principles of justice, without undue delay. And women who are political prisoners, including Yasmin Rashid and Bushra Bibi, should be released expeditiously on humanitarian grounds.” Effective, continuous and meaningful consultation between the federal and provincial governments to eradicate terrorism, protect the lives and property of the people and establish lasting peace in KP. “Existing policies and measures should be reviewed and amended as needed.” Authorised representatives of the federal and provincial governments shall convene regular meetings within 72 hours and, through mutual consultation, formulate a clear, comprehensive and feasible strategy for peace and security. The implementation of this strategy, within the scope of the Constitution and law, shall be the joint responsibility of the federal and provincial governments.” The KP CM said that PTI would announce the cancellation of the long march upon receiving a written assurance from the federal government for the effective implementation of the aforementioned assurances and agreed actions. “However, if the federal government violates the agreed assurances, the negotiation process, or constitutional and legal requirements, or causes undue disruption to the negotiation process, PTI shall reserve the right to peaceful, democratic and lawful protest in accordance with the Constitution and law”, he added. Responding to Afridi on X, Naqvi said the “negotiating teams finalised a separate draft with us, which both sides agreed to, in addition to the KP Terrorism Related Implementation Plan”. Commenting on that, KP Information Minister Shafiullah Jan said the PTI’s negotiating committee “came with a full mandate that we would endorse every decision they made, however they deemed fit”. “The provincial government’s mandate lies with the chief minister. The KP government’s policy cannot go against Imran Khan’s ideology. Your intent is not to end terrorism but to end PTI,” Jan asserted. “The blood of our innocent Pakhtuns is not so cheap that, under your misguided policies, we would sacrifice another 80,000 lives. Terrorism has been forcibly imposed on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Those who start the fire can never put it out,” he claimed. The provincial minister stressed that a policy shift regarding counterterrorism was necessary as “relying solely on the policy of guns and batons will not work”. “A few self-proclaimed wise men sitting in closed rooms will not decide our future,” Jan said. PPP says KP govt ‘began dictating terms’ PPP Senator Sherry Rehman, who was part of the talks, also blamed the KP chief minister, saying the talks “collapsed on the KP government’s unilateral refusal to sign the afternoon’s pre-agreed draft on counterterrorism cooperation with the Centre”. In a post on X, she emphasised that the idea behind the agreement was to bring the province on board on all counterterrorism actions. The PPP leader said the government’s team had repeatedly asked for the provincial government of KP to be in the talks as well, but the chief minister or cabinet representatives did not turn up. “If they had a viable draft, they should have shown up themselves or communicated it to their committee over the two days, without constant reversals”, she added. “No point presenting new drafts on social media after refusing to show up or sabotaging their own teams by broadcasting messages that subvert the process,” Rehman stated. The senior politician went on to say: “I have never in my 25 years in parliament seen such a reckless squandering of an opening to begin political CBMs (confidence-building measures), and to bring stability to Pakistan after years of bitter political division.” Rehman regretted that instead of “taking the opportunity the PPP-govt team offered them to unlock the blind alley they have taken themselves into, their Peshawar government began dictating terms after 8:30pm when all but final agreements had been signed”. “We really went more than halfway. The rest could have followed.”

items.title: Cheikh Hamidou Kane, l’auteur de «L’Aventure ambiguë», s’éteint à 98 ans
items.description: L’écrivain, haut fonctionnaire et ancien ministre sénégalais Cheikh Hamidou Kane, figure majeure des lettres africaines et auteur du célèbre roman «L’Aventure ambiguë», est décédé, le samedi 3 octobre 2026 au soir à Dakar, à l’âge de 98 ans. Sa disparition a notamment été annoncée par le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Le Sénégal perd l’une de ses grandes figures intellectuelles. Cheikh Hamidou Kane, dont le nom reste intimement lié à «L’Aventure ambiguë», classique de la littérature africaine publié en 1961 aux Éditions Julliard et Présence africaine, s’est éteint à Dakar à l’âge de 98 ans. Le président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Faye a rendu hommage à l’illustre disparu dans un message publié sur sa page Facebook. «J’ai appris avec une profonde tristesse le rappel à Dieu de Cheikh Hamidou Kane», a écrit le chef de l’État. À travers son œuvre majeure, l’écrivain a notamment interrogé le rapport de l’Afrique au savoir, à la modernité et à ses propres valeurs. Une réflexion dont la portée demeure actuelle, selon le président sénégalais. «Avec ‘L’Aventure ambiguë’, il a donné à des générations d’Africains les mots pour penser une question qui nous habite encore, celle de s’ouvrir au savoir du monde sans rien perdre de ce que nous sommes. Ministre de la République, il a aussi servi le Sénégal avec dévouement», a témoigné le chef de l’État. Bassirou Diomaye Faye a adressé ses condoléances à la famille et aux proches du défunt, ainsi qu’à l’ensemble du monde des lettres. «Son œuvre appartient désormais au patrimoine de notre nation et de toute l’Afrique», a-t-il écrit. Une œuvre qui a traversé les générations Né en 1928 à Matam, dans le nord du Sénégal, Cheikh Hamidou Kane s’est imposé comme l’une des grandes voix de la littérature africaine d’expression française. Publié en 1961, «L’Aventure ambiguë» lui a valu, dès 1962, le Grand Prix littéraire d’Afrique noire. Le roman, traduit dans plusieurs langues, s’est progressivement imposé comme un incontournable de la littérature africaine et continue d’être étudié dans de nombreux établissements scolaires et universitaires. À travers le parcours de son personnage principal, Samba Diallo, l’œuvre met en tension plusieurs univers de pensée et explore notamment les rapports entre tradition et modernité, identité culturelle et ouverture au monde. Mais Cheikh Hamidou Kane n’était pas seulement un homme de lettres. Haut fonctionnaire et homme politique, il a également consacré une importante partie de sa vie au service de l’État sénégalais. Il a notamment occupé les fonctions de ministre du Développement industriel et de l’Artisanat, puis celles de ministre du Plan et de la Coopération. «Les Gardiens du temple», autre héritage littéraire Le défunt laisse également derrière lui «Les Gardiens du temple», publié aux Éditions Stock en 1997. Dans ce roman, l’auteur revient sur les défis auxquels est confronté un jeune État africain indépendant, partagé entre la volonté d’affirmer son identité et l’influence persistante de l’Occident. Par son œuvre littéraire comme par son parcours au service de la République, Cheikh Hamidou Kane aura ainsi marqué plusieurs générations au Sénégal et au-delà des frontières du pays. Son empreinte institutionnelle demeure également visible.L’Université virtuelle du Sénégal a été baptisée à son nom sous la présidence de Macky Sall, qui a dirigé le pays de 2012 à 2024. Un héritage qui dépasse les frontières du Sénégal À 98 ans, Cheikh Hamidou Kane laisse donc derrière lui une œuvre qui a largement dépassé le cadre sénégalais. «L’Aventure ambiguë», en particulier, demeure l’un des textes emblématiques de la littérature africaine, par sa réflexion sur l’identité, le savoir et la rencontre entre les cultures. Avec sa disparition, le Sénégal perd un écrivain majeur, mais l’Afrique voit surtout s’éteindre l’une de ses grandes voix intellectuelles. Son œuvre, elle, devrait continuer à interroger les générations sur la délicate recherche d’un équilibre entre ouverture au monde et fidélité à soi. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Cheikh Hamidou Kane, l’auteur de «L’Aventure ambiguë», s’éteint à 98 ans est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: The Traffitech-GH SMS spot-fine system: The good, the sad, and the funny – Bright Simons writes
items.description: The carnage on Ghana’s roads is not a joke. Road crashes killed 2,949 people in 2025, up from 2,494 the year before. Serious injuries rose to 16,714. Many people believe that bad motorist behaviour has a big part to play, and that the Police are either too stretched thin or too corrupt to effectively enforce deterrence. So when the government announces that it is deploying technology to improve the situation, it is hard to argue with the logic. However, there were some murmurings about poor sensitisation. The Police took the cue and postponed implementation by a month. We now have to wait until 1st November 2026 before the police start fining motorists by text message. Cameras and handheld devices will catch vehicles speeding, jumping red lights, and committing more than 45 other offences, and the registered owner will get an SMS with the fine and 14 days to pay. How are we going to use the one month to influence how the program shapes up? On my part, I see a teaching moment for katanomics (www dot katanomics dot org). The katanomic framing of the SMS-spot-finding initiative is that, as usual, the political vision is easy to sell (stop road carnage). It is a simple WHAT message that rallies the people. The HOW – the realm of POLICY – is where things usually start falling apart. Because POLICY takes a simple goal and unravels it into many complex parts, some of which are in tension. THE DEVIL IS ALWAYS IN THE DETAIL. Since you’ve read up to this point, you asked for it. 1. The journey to the Traffitech-GH system surprisingly started around 2008, nearly 20 years ago. Implementation of the idea of using cameras to catch traffic violators and issue spot fines has had a bumpy ride. 2. The person who has kept it going is a gritty entrepreneur who has survived the NPP – NDC rollercoaster that has quenched so many business dreams. His name is Frank Osei. The heart of his empire is Nationwide Technologies. 3. He sold the tax stamps and fuel marking to the NDC in the Mills era. The NDC were slow to get either to a serious scale. The NPP came and bulldozed them through. He pushed the public-private partnership (PPP) concession for the text-messaging spot-fine system during the NPP era and helped get the agreement signed in 2022. The NPP was sluggish in deploying it. The NDC seems determined to bulldoze it through. 4. As I said, Mr Osei set up Nationwide Traffic Management & Enforcement Limited (NTMEL) in 2008 and started pushing aggressively. As was the case with the tax stamps and fuel marking projects he helped broker with the government, he ended up needing a foreign technology partner from Sweden, a company called Sensys Gatso. 5. The origin of Sensys Gatso is actually in 1950s Holland, where a relentless speed-racing driver, Maurice Gatsonides, decided to invent an automated speed-tracking technology to sustain his impossibly high standards. 6. Sensys Gatso’s TRaaS and related technologies will, initially, be deployed in Ghana primarily in the form of fixed cameras at about 34 hazardous junctions, ~20 in-vehicle cameras, ~30 handheld laser cameras, and tripod units to record offences. 7. Officers also log offences on handheld devices. Images will go to regional back offices, where police review them before a notice is sent by SMS from “GPS-MTTD”. Owners can pay through http://Ghana.gov , mobile money or *222#, or contest online and attend a hearing at an MTTD station. MTTD is Ghana’s transport police. 8. Camera fines start at GH¢120 for the first three offences, then GH¢180 and GH¢240. A sixth offence within 24 months can go to court and cost a licence for at least a year. After 14 days, 1 per cent of the fine is added every day, so an unpaid GH¢120 fine becomes GH¢240 after 100 days of default. No cap has been published. Unpaid fines can block DVLA services, and officials have floated restrictions linked to the Ghana Card. The registered owner is liable “regardless of who was driving”. 10. The first time Ghana really got serious about doing this was in 2016 when an agreement was reached to deploy in 2017. In April 2018, the President’s road-safety action plan directed a partnership with “private towing companies and NTMEL.” GH¢335 million a year was promised for three years, partly to pay for road signs and markings, and the techie stuff. The towing scheme collapsed that year. The rest crumbled on cue, though some people got “warning text messages.” 11. By the end of 2021, the Ministry of Finance listed the project as an unsolicited proposal under negotiation at an estimated US$9.9 million. 12. As mentioned earlier, the current PPP agreement was signed on 23 December 2022 for eleven years (to December 2033) with a reported investment cost of GH¢77.73 million (about $7.3 million then). Caution notices began in June 2024, and by the end of 2025, about 120,000 had been sent. 13. The law itself came last. The Road Traffic (Amendment) Act, passed in December 2025, mentions automated enforcement once, by adding that a “spot fine” includes an automated fine. Owner liability, the daily surcharge, licence penalties and camera evidence are all perching in regulations passed in 2026 (L.I. 2519). 14. Note the classic katanomics: the contract, whose economics depend on fines, was signed three years before the state had the regulations to levy them. 15. I find it puzzling that Police and ministers seem so guarded about explaining this history. They regularly refer to “a private sector partner” and provide no further details. 16. Yet Sensys Gatso has been very open about the whole commercial apparatus. 17. NTMEL’s shares are split exactly 60 per cent to Mr Frank Osei and 40 per cent to Sensys Gatso International B.V., part of the Swedish-listed Sensys Gatso Group, as aforementioned. 18. The Ghanaian majority is, however, only part of the picture. The Board is split right down the middle. Lewis H. Miller, who became chief executive of Sensys Gatso Group in June 2025, and Timo Gatsonides, one of Sensys Gatso’s largest shareholders, hold the fort for the Swedes on NTMEL’s 4-person Director list. NTMEL’s managing director, Edmar van der Weijden, is also managing director of Sensys Gatso International, the 40 per cent shareholder. A former Sensys Gatso chief executive is registered as a beneficial owner of NTMEL with the right to appoint and remove directors. 20. Sensys Gatso also supplies the cameras and software, and has said it expects to earn from hardware sales and licence fees on top of its share of profits. 21. Like the Margins-run “Ghana Card”, the whole Traffitech-GH scheme is fundamentally commercial. The revenue comes from fining people and is split 40 per cent to the private party and 60 per cent to government. That is to say, if you are dumb enough to text whilst driving, you will be putting a cool ~50 GHS into the pocket of Mr Osei and his Swedish partners for each text. 22. Sensys Gatso has told its investors to expect about SEK 600 million (~$60 million) in joint-venture revenue over the rest of the contract. Its 2025 annual report shows NTMEL had no revenue in 2024 or 2025, lost SEK 5.9 million (~$600k) in 2025, and ended the year with SEK 2.9 million in cash. The operator needs fines to flow. 23. The government’s 2022 PPP report lists “revenues from traffic fines for Government” among the benefits it expects to maximise. Finance Ministry mandarins are sitting there with a calculator waiting for clowns to jump red lights. 24. I will admit it, I am a bit uneasy about this. Not because I have sympathy for red-light jumpers. I just think that when the operator’s income rises with every fine-ticket, the pressure is to put cameras where tickets are plentiful rather than where people die, to tighten thresholds of offending, and to resist appeals. 25. Uganda’s version of this model reportedly gave its foreign operator 80 per cent of fines and was suspended within days of launch in June 2025 because of such perverse incentives. 26. I also think that the investors have been waiting to rake in revenue before bothering to invest. The whole operation feels too barebones given the scale of the problem. It is true that Ghana already has thousands of outdoor cameras. But these are Chinese-vendor-supplied national security cameras that are unsuitable for Traffitech-GH for many reasons, including privacy and the lack of special traffic-monitoring-focused features. This means NTMEL must deploy a ton of cameras and personnel to review the footage/images. So far, they appear to be waiting for the fine revenue to go through the roof before doing this. I also worry about enforcement quality. Sending a text message to people in a country like Ghana to pay a fine is literally daring them to ignore, wait, and see. Would we then rely on the same Police we are replacing with tech due to their supposed ineptitude, incapacity, and/or corruption to go around forcing people to pay? 28. The idea of hooking this up to drivers’ licenses and Ghana Card sounds brilliant in theory, but it runs heavily into the serious informality that attends every aspect of our lives in Ghana. Unlike elsewhere, people don’t have to encounter the formal system regularly to survive. The same reason why, despite repeated “mass registrations”, we keep hearing that the Ghana Card system is porous is the reason why relying on civil identity platforms would, in my humble view, prove less robust than we think. 29. The 2024 pilots showed that missing owner information in DVLA records, and insurance records still bearing brokers’ phone numbers instead of owners’, are rather pervasive issues. Vehicles registered by hand before 2023 are still being re-verified. So, anyone who sold a car without completing the transfer, or changed their number, may learn of a fine only once penalties have piled up. 30. Seven people were arrested in February 2026 for sending FAKE fine notices with payment links. The scammers are already ahead of the system. 31. Another issue is that disputes go to MTTD stations. There is no independent body, unlike South Africa, where a separate agency adjudicates. So, we are back to making this a Police gig. 32. I worry that the basics may not even be in place. Speed enforcement is fair only where limits are posted. Red-light enforcement is smooth only where signals work. Where the infrastructure itself seems designed to promote disorderly behaviour, we may yet find that the system regularly gets overwhelmed by the sheer volumes of recorded violations. 33. It seems very clear to me that the government, and the Police in particular, have a fine one-month opportunity to show that they can rise above katanomics. There are several things they can do to do so. 34. They can publish the PPP contract for further scrutiny; change the terms from a share of fines to a fixed fee to discourage overzealous and commercially minded deployment; tighten the law to avoid abuse of the system to track and spy on people (ensuring that images aren’t passed around to jealous husbands or something, for instance); implement an independent appeals process; publish a risk-based deployment map (i.e. investment in cameras etc., should follow what the data says about the highest risk of road crashes); and outline a safeguarding measure against scams and fraud. 35. Will the Police beat katanomics? Who is up for a bet? – Authored by: Bright Simons

items.title: Équipe nationale : les cadres n’ont pas dit leur dernier mot
items.description: Le Sénégal s’est imposé (1-0) ce dimanche au Vélodrome face aux Comores, dans un match amical qui aura servi de laboratoire à Patrick Vieira. Si le sélectionneur a voulu voir à l’œuvre de nouveaux visages, les anciens ont, eux, envoyé un message sans ambiguïté. Gana Gueye et Kalidou Koulibaly, solides et influents, ont rappelé qu’ils n’entendaient pas regarder la nouvelle génération prendre les commandes depuis le banc. Les cadres sont toujours là, et ils comptent bien le faire savoir. Si les jeunes poussent derrière, les cadres, eux, n’ont visiblement aucune intention de leur dérouler le tapis rouge. Face aux Comores, certains ont même profité de cette fenêtre internationale pour rappeler qu’ils avaient encore de solides arguments à faire valoir. Gana Gueye encore au-dessus de la mêlée À 37 ans, Idrissa Gana Gueye n’a manifestement pas l’intention de passer le relais aussi facilement. Titulaire face aux Comores, le milieu d’Al Diriyah a encore affiché cette activité et cette maîtrise qui ont longtemps fait de lui un incontournable des Lions. Son rendement contraste avec celui de certains concurrents plus jeunes. Lamine Camara, notamment, n’a pas totalement convaincu durant cette fenêtre internationale. Après avoir longtemps été présenté comme l’un des futurs patrons du milieu sénégalais, le Monégasque a vu son influence diminuer au fil des rencontres. De quoi relancer une hiérarchie que l’on croyait appelée à évoluer rapidement. Pour l’heure, Gana reste donc bien placé. Son expérience, son volume de jeu et sa capacité à donner du rythme continuent de peser dans les choix du sélectionneur. Patrick Vieira voulait voir si les anciens avaient encore leur mot à dire. Gana Gueye vient de lui apporter une réponse assez claire. Koulibaly remet la pression Même constat derrière. Face aux Comores, Kalidou Koulibaly (35 ans) a retrouvé le brassard de patron de la défense et surtout une place dans un secteur où la concurrence s’est considérablement rajeunie. Associé à Mamadou Sarr dans l’axe, le capitaine historique a livré une prestation suffisamment solide pour rappeler qu’il n’était pas disposé à laisser sa place sans résistance. La situation est d’autant plus intéressante que la concurrence semble désormais se préciser. Sadibou Sané apparaît comme une option sérieuse dans la hiérarchie, tandis que Koulibaly revient dans la discussion pour accompagner ou concurrencer le défenseur de Villarreal. Dans cette configuration, Mamadou Sarr pourrait être le principal perdant de cette redistribution des cartes. Le Sénégal dispose désormais de plusieurs profils pour le poste de défenseur central droit, et la bataille pourrait se jouer entre Sadibou Sané et Kalidou Koulibaly pour le rôle de titulaire, avec Mamadou Sarr en embuscade. Le message envoyé par Koulibaly est finalement le même que celui de Gana Gueye. Le renouvellement générationnel voulu par Vieira ne signifie pas encore la fin du règne des anciens. Les cadres sont toujours debout, toujours compétitifs et surtout toujours candidats à une place dans le onze. Par Yaya SOW

items.title: Face à l’agression américaine, l’Iran travaille à augmenter la portée de ses missiles
items.description: L'Iran a engage des travaux pour augmenter la portee de ses missiles balistiques, apres l'agression americaine. Le porte-parole de l'armee iranienne, Mohammad Akraminia, est cite ce 4 octobre par l'agence Fars : « Au cours de cette guerre [avec les etats-Unis], nous avons conclu qu'il etait imperatif d'augmenter la portee de nos missiles et nous y travaillons actuellement. » Le porte-parole explique cette decision par l'eloignement des navires de l'US Navy, desormais deployes jusqu'a 1 000 kilometres des cotes iraniennes. L'armee de la Republique islamique juge donc necessaire d'augmenter la portee de ses armes pour pouvoir atteindre ces bâtiments en cas de nouvelle attaque americaine. Des ameliorations sur les missiles de croisiere et les missiles navals La portee n'est qu'un volet des travaux. Le porte-parole annonce egalement des ameliorations de la vitesse et de la precision, notamment pour les missiles de croisiere a longue portee et les missiles navals employes contre les bâtiments ennemis. L'Iran s'est deja servi de ses missiles et de ses drones pour repondre aux attaques americaines. Apres le debut de l'agression des etats-Unis et d'Israel, le 28 fevrier, les ripostes iraniennes ont notamment vise les bases americaines au Moyen-Orient. L'accord de juin devait interrompre ces hostilites. Pourtant, des juillet, Washington a repris ses frappes et Teheran a de nouveau riposte, notamment contre les bases au Koweït et a Bahreïn. Les tirs iraniens se sont repetes durant l'ete. En septembre, une nouvelle riposte a suivi les attaques americaines contre le Sistan-et-Baloutchistan et l'Hormozgan. Esmaïl Baghaï, porte-parole du ministere iranien des Affaires etrangeres, a egalement averti ce 4 octobre les pays dont le territoire pourrait servir a de nouvelles attaques americaines et israeliennes contre l'Iran : « La riposte sera incontestablement d'une tout autre nature. » Un accord reclame sous la menace Washington cherche aujourd'hui a obtenir un accord tout en menacant l'Iran. Lors d'un deplacement au Texas, le 2 octobre, Donald Trump a evoque l'elimination des autorites iraniennes si elles refusaient les conditions americaines. Il a pourtant envisage un reglement avant les elections de mi-mandat de novembre, ou peu apres. Sur les negociations, Esmaïl Baghaï affirme que Teheran a refuse de laisser Washington imposer le dossier nucleaire a l'ordre du jour : « La transmission des reponses claires et fermes de l'Iran aux propositions de la partie americaine, par l'intermediaire du mediateur qatari a Doha, a demontre l'echec des tentatives de Washington visant a detourner les negociations vers le dossier nucleaire. » L'Iran reclame notamment la levee des sanctions americaines pour retablir une navigation sûre dans le detroit d'Ormuz.

items.title: Puffins
items.description: The wind brings the circus to a lonesome town upstate, and puffins to the Isle of May, seagirt, desolate. The wind brings spectators by ferry to the docks. Side by side like gravy boats seals loll on the rocks. The throng swipes their shoes on a disinfectant mat, running down the gangplank to the puffins’ habitat. The main ring is the breeding ground where lies their single egg circled with a constant cry echoed off the crag. They circle, circle, swoop, and dive, coming back with silver sprats like spiny roses in the teeth of undefeated acrobats. The comic masks they wear belie the effort it must take to migrate all their lives in search of a decent windbreak. Clown-bright lichen clothes the rocks, sea campion froths in grass. Here’s the roofless abbey on a speck in the atlas. This poem appears in the November 2026 print edition.

items.title: AI’s Real Gift to Science
items.description: Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, has often said that AI will cure most diseases in the next 10 years. Late last month, he claimed that his company had taken a first step toward that future: Claude had, in less than 24 hours, discovered a new “enzyme system” that the company says resembles CRISPR, a gene-editing tool currently curing people of diseases. While announcing the discovery, Anthropic hinted that this was the type of finding that revolutionizes medicine and quoted a gene-editing pioneer who called it “genuinely intriguing.” The company was open about not knowing what exactly it had spotted or whether the finding—the first released from a biology lab that the company established this spring—was really that significant. Still, many academics, along with the CEO of Eli Lilly, pointed out that the company had dressed up a very incremental finding as a major discovery. Fyodor Urnov, a scientist who coined the term genome editing and is working on a CRISPR project with Anthropic, told me that “the jury is out” on whether what Claude found is even an enzyme at all. Multiple researchers told The New York Times that, in fact, they had been aware of the supposedly new enzyme system for years, including a team at the University of Copenhagen that alleged Anthropic’s new results might have been stolen from their lab’s interactions with Claude. The company, in response, said that Claude isn’t trained using user transcripts. (Anthropic did not respond to a comment request for this article.) In other words, Anthropic made a big deal about a finding that—although achieved in a novel, Claude-led way—may not lead to any biomedical advances, and that the company knew may not lead to any biomedical advances. Ironically, in making such grandiose statements, the company and other AI boosters obscured what Claude does appear to have accomplished: It sorted through reams of biological data that would have taken scientists much longer to analyze, if they could have at all. This capacity might not be a miracle, but for scientists facing mountains of data that have surpassed their capacity for analysis, it’s still meaningful. Around the turn of the 21st century, researchers sequenced for the first time all 3 billion letters that make up human DNA. This effort, called the Human Genome Project, took 13 years and cost $2.7 billion. Today, sequencing a person’s full genome takes just over a day and costs as little as $200. Accordingly, the total amount of publicly available genomic data has become so large as to be unmanageable. In other fields, such as protein science, technological advances have led to a similar boom in the sheer amount of data being collected. Trying to pull anything useful from all that data has become its own long-term project. In 2012, a committee of bioinformatics experts found that the “bottleneck in scientific productivity” had moved from data production to data analysis, but early efforts at the National Institutes of Health to deal with that bottleneck quickly sputtered out. If researchers could efficiently store, send, and examine all of the information they generated, they would likely be able to, for example, develop new drugs by identifying better genes or cellular parts to target. But it’s simply too massive for them to comprehensively attack. The biological corpus is not, however, too large for AI agents. Bo Wang, an assistant professor at the University of Toronto and the chief AI scientist at a drug-discovery company, recently wrote that AI’s biggest impact in biology will come from its help “scaling scientific attention”: Setting agents loose on the enormous data sets can surface the outliers that warrant further human inspection. Agents can propose and test hypotheses for what might cause the unusual patterns they find, and predictive modeling can help scientists choose what experiments to carry out on their actual lab benches. Eventually, automated labs might even carry out those chosen experiments—a few already exist in the United States, and the Trump administration is spending hundreds of millions to establish more. Meanwhile, scientists remain divided over whether AI models actually steer them toward potentially paradigm-shifting experiments, or safer, less exploratory ones. AI is already changing medicine: Models that use people’s medical history to predict their health risks, including their likelihood of developing certain kinds of cancer, are now used in most U.S. hospitals. At the same time, not every field of biology generates enough data for this approach to work. AI might be less useful in some domains that rely on less abundant microscopy data, such as the study of how cells and tissues communicate; such data tend to be harder to come by than genetic sequences, Stirling Churchman, a professor of genetics at Harvard Medical School, told me. Organelle biology and the science of cellular transport similarly require painstaking, time-consuming experiments. Still, Churchman said, “there will be magic where there’s data.” She spent the summer at OpenAI working on a specially trained model for life-science researchers. She anticipates that by allowing scientists who can’t code to examine their data themselves, AI will enable researchers to “analyze data at least 10 times faster, freeing us to spend more time on the biological questions and experiments.” The recent Anthropic finding is an example of how AI can identify outliers that might otherwise have gone unnoticed. Existing tools can comb through heaps of genomic data (and have already been used to identify bona fide new gene-editing systems). What AI can do is run those kinds of analyses at a much larger scale, while also evaluating intermediary results, Kendell Clement, who runs a computational-biology lab at the University of Utah, told me. Of course, that scale requires dumping in correspondingly huge resources: Anthropic directed about 950 Claude bots to simultaneously pore over a database that contained nearly 2 billion DNA entries. AI companies have every incentive to keep evangelizing about the medical miracles they say their models will unlock, especially as backlash against them mounts. Amodei has an idea for how to quiet AI skeptics: “The thing that will work is actually curing cancer,” he recently wrote on X. That would certainly be a coup. But helping scientists work more quickly is, too, even if it doesn’t sound quite so revolutionary.

items.title: Football : le Sénégal bat les Comores 1-0 en match amical
items.description: L’équipe nationale de football du Sénégal s’est imposée face aux Comores (1-0), dimanche au stade Vélodrome de Marseille, en match amical international. Les Lions ont assuré l’essentiel grâce à un but d’Iliman Ndiaye inscrit dès les premières minutes de la rencontre. Les hommes de Patrick Vieira ont rapidement pris le contrôle des opérations. Iliman Ndiaye a ouvert le score à la 5e minute, sur une action initiée par Ibrahim Mbaye, permettant au Sénégal de concrétiser sa bonne entame. Après cette ouverture du score, les Lions ont conservé leur avantage jusqu’à la pause. Le sélectionneur Patrick Vieira avait procédé à plusieurs changements dans son onze de départ, offrant notamment du temps de jeu à des joueurs moins sollicités lors des deux premières rencontres de la fenêtre internationale. Kalidou Koulibaly, capitaine, a notamment été titularisé en défense centrale aux côtés de Mamadou Sarr. En seconde période, le Sénégal a continué à maîtriser la rencontre sans parvenir à inscrire un deuxième but. Les Comoriens n’ont pas réussi à revenir au score et les Lions ont finalement conservé leur avantage jusqu’au coup de sifflet final. Cette victoire permet au Sénégal de conclure sa fenêtre internationale sur une note positive, après un match nul contre le Mozambique (1-1) et une victoire contre l’Éthiopie (1-0) dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Pour Patrick Vieira, cette rencontre aura également permis d’évaluer plusieurs joueurs et de poursuivre les ajustements de son équipe en perspective des prochaines échéances internationales.
